SECTION A 
Technical Build 

A1. System Design & Architecture 
Individual docs/<student-name>/use-cases.md Define use cases for all user roles. Each use case should name the actor, trigger, main flow, and any edge-case or alternative flows. 
Individual docs/<student-name>/api-documentation.md Document every API endpoint: method, path, example request body, expected response, and error codes returned. 
Individual docs/<student-name>/database-schema.md Include an entity-relationship diagram or table definitions showing all fields, types, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships. 
Group docs/architecture.md Describe the overall system architecture: what each layer does, how the components interact, technology choices, and how to navigate the project structure. Keep this file updated to reflect the final build. 
Group docs/architecture-diagram.png A visual diagram of the full system (frontend → backend → database → storage). Export as PNG and reference it from architecture.md. Should match the final deployed system. 
A2. Code Implementation & Integration 
Individual frontend/src/ React components, pages, hooks, and utilities. Each team member's individual contributions should be traceable through Git commit history. 
Individual backend/src/ Routes, controllers, models, and middleware. Auth and protected routes must be implemented. No credentials or secrets committed — use .env.example instead. 
Group Git history The shared repository must show a clear branching strategy (e.g. feature branches → main), meaningful commit messages, and evidence of merge conflict resolution. All team members should have regular individual commits. 
A3. Testing & Deployment 
Individual tests/<student-name>/ Unit tests for your individual code contributions. Test files should be clear, well-named, and include meaningful assertions. All tests must pass before submission. Multiple test files are allowed within your folder. 
Group README.md Must include: (1) how to run the project locally, (2) how to deploy, and (3) the public URL of the deployed app. Keep it up to date — tutors will use this to verify deployment.

**The project in one breath:** A five-person full-stack app (React + Node + DB) for SCCCI to run real-time attendance/headcount for overseas delegations, built around the "Reverse Headcount" idea (show who's *missing*, not who's present). **Your patch (Jayden) — Exception Logging & QR Scanning.** Your CRUD entity is **Support Tickets**, and you own two enhanced capabilities:

- **Exception/issue logging (CRUD):** log, read, resolve, and cancel on-the-ground tickets — lost badge, missing person, face-match failed, dead phone, VIP request.
- **Enhanced #1 — real-time cross-device alerting:** when a *critical* ticket is raised, it instantly pushes to all staff devices. This is your standout piece and it directly answers the client's single biggest fear (a missing person causing a "programme overrun").
- **Enhanced #2 — QR code as the fallback identification** method, plus a **manual attendance override** ("tap to count" when a phone is dead / face scan fails).
- Your endpoints: `POST /api/exceptions`, `GET /api/exceptions/active`, `PATCH /api/exceptions/{id}/resolve`, and `PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override`.

Your four screens map cleanly onto that: the **Exception Inbox** (admin/web) is your CRUD *read* view plus the alert banner; **QR Fallback**, **Log Exception**, and **Critical Alert** (mobile, on-ground staff) are your scan fallback, ticket *create*, and the *receive* side of your real-time alert. The set is genuinely complete and on-brief — it covers CRUD *and* both enhancements, which is exactly what the rubric rewards.

**The reality check that changes your strategy.** The rubric is **80 marks individual / 20 group**. Your distinction is almost entirely in your own hands, and — this is the important part — **your Figma being done doesn't score directly.** There's no "design" line item. Design is a means; the marks live in a *working, integrated system* and your own documents. So most of your grade is still ahead of you:

- **A1 (15):** your own `use-cases.md`, `api-documentation.md`, `database-schema.md`. For an "A" these must cover *all roles + edge cases*, document every endpoint with example request + error codes, and show a normalised schema with all relationships.
- **A2 (25, your biggest bucket):** your actual React + Node + DB code for exceptions/QR, with auth + protected routes, plus regular, meaningful Git commits.
- **A3 (10):** your unit tests (well-named, meaningful assertions, all passing) + group deployment.
- **B1 (10) + B2 (15):** how you personally demo and field questions.
- **C1 (10) + C2 (10):** your AI logs across *all* phases and a reflective write-up — a full fifth of the grade, all individual, and the most commonly under-invested.

**The distinction playbook for your part specifically:**

1. **Make the real-time alert your showpiece.** It's the hardest thing you own (WebSocket/SSE push) and the highest-value. Nail it and you hit the A-grade descriptor "adds tangible value." Plan now how you'll *demo* it convincingly across two devices.
2. **Show the offline edge case.** Your own manual-override use case says: no roaming data → save locally and queue-sync later. Demonstrating that offline queue live is a direct hit on B2's "edge cases and error states handled gracefully" — a classic distinction separator.
3. **Start the AI logs today.** C1/C2 = 20 marks and reward strategic, iterative use *across design → coding → testing → deployment*, with evidence you rejected or reshaped AI output. Because it must span all phases, the only way to score well is to log from the very first task — which is the real reason "start ASAP" matters.
4. **Coordinate your boundary with Vimal.** His `/api/attendance/scan` and your QR fallback + manual override touch the same attendance records. Agree the contract early to avoid a messy integration (which the rubric penalises).
5. **Deployment gotchas:** QR scanning needs the camera, which requires HTTPS — Vercel gives you that. Render's free tier sleeps after 15 min and takes ~30s to wake; warn your tutor/client before the demo.

You want to start now, so rather than keep talking, I'd rather build you the first real deliverable. The highest-leverage starting point is your **A1 document set** (use-cases, API docs, DB schema for tickets + manual override) — it's a required submission, it forces the design decisions your code will follow, and drafting it *with* me becomes your first AI-workflow log entry. Which would you like me to draft first?

input.file_text:
# Use Cases — Exception Logging, QR Fallback & Manual Override

**Module:** Full Stack Application Development (2026S1)
**Project:** SCCCI Delegation Attendance System ("MusterGo")
**Author:** Jayden
**Feature area:** Exception & Issue Logging (Support Tickets CRUD) · QR-code fallback identification · Real-time critical alerting · Manual attendance override
**Rubric mapping:** A1 System Design & Architecture (Individual)

---

## 1. Scope & Ownership

This document defines the use cases for the feature set I own. It covers three user roles and the system itself as an actor (for automated alert fan-out).

| Actor | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **On-site Staff** | Mobile-app user on the ground (lobby, coach, venue). Logs exceptions, scans QR as a fallback, performs manual overrides, receives and acknowledges alerts. |
| **Administrator** | Web-dashboard user. Monitors and triages the Exception Inbox, resolves/cancels tickets, watches critical alerts. |
| **System** | The application itself. Automatically fans out critical alerts to all staff devices and queues offline actions for later sync. |

**Integration boundary (noted for the assessor):** the shared check-in write path (`POST /api/attendance/scan`, accepting face-hash *or* QR payload) is owned by Vimal. My QR capability is the *fallback client flow* that consumes that shared contract and, on failure, routes into my exception-logging and manual-override paths. Endpoints I own are listed in `api-documentation.md`.

**Enumerations referenced below** (defined fully in `database-schema.md`):
- `issue_type`: `MISSING_PERSON`, `LOST_BADGE`, `FACE_MATCH_FAILED`, `DEAD_PHONE`, `VIP_REQUEST`, `OTHER`
- `priority`: `CRITICAL`, `NORMAL`, `LOW`
- `status`: `OPEN`, `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED`
- `ack_status`: `PENDING`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `ON_IT`

---

## UC-01 — Log an on-ground exception

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | A delegate cannot check in normally (lost badge, dead phone, face-match failure, VIP need) and staff taps **Log exception** on the mobile app. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; a trip is active; staff has the delegate in view or knows their identity. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff opens the **Log exception** screen (Screen 10).
2. Staff selects an **issue type** (e.g. *Lost badge*).
3. Staff selects the affected **delegate** from the trip roster (or leaves it blank for an unidentified person).
4. Staff adds an optional **quick note** (e.g. "Phone unreachable, last seen near gift shop 14:08").
5. Staff leaves **Mark as critical** off for a normal-priority issue and taps **Submit**.
6. System creates the ticket with `status = OPEN`, `priority = NORMAL`, returns the new `issueId`, and the ticket appears in the admin **Exception Inbox** (Screen 5).

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A1a — Offline:** device has no roaming data. System saves the ticket to a local queue, shows an "offline — will sync" indicator, and submits automatically once connectivity returns (idempotent by client-generated `clientRef`).
- **A1b — Missing required field:** no issue type selected. System blocks submission and shows an inline validation error (maps to `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`).
- **A1c — Unidentified person:** no delegate chosen. Ticket is created with `delegate_id = null` and a free-text description; can be linked to a delegate later.

**Postconditions**
A support ticket exists, is visible to all staff/admin, and is queryable in the inbox.

---

## UC-02 — Raise a critical missing-person alert (real-time fan-out)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff (raises) · System (dispatches) |
| **Trigger** | Staff logs an exception with **Mark as critical** enabled — typically a *missing person* before an imminent departure. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; a trip is active; at least one other staff device is registered to the trip. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff selects issue type **Missing person**, chooses the delegate (e.g. *Lim Wei Jie · Coach 2 · VIP*), and enables **Mark as critical — alerts all staff devices instantly**.
2. Staff taps **Submit & alert team**.
3. System creates the ticket with `priority = CRITICAL`, `status = OPEN`.
4. System fans out a **critical alert** to every registered staff device on the trip (Screen 11), creating one `exception_alert` row per recipient with `ack_status = PENDING`.
5. The admin dashboard banner updates instantly ("1 critical exception · pushed to all N staff devices").

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A2a — No recipients online:** alerts are queued and delivered on reconnect; the raiser still sees "sent, awaiting delivery".
- **A2b — Duplicate critical for same delegate:** system detects an existing `OPEN` critical ticket for that delegate on that trip and appends to it rather than creating a duplicate (prevents alert spam).
- **A2c — Delegate already resolved elsewhere:** if the delegate was checked in on another device moments earlier, the alert still sends but is flagged "possible false alarm — last seen boarded 14:09" so staff can stand down quickly.

**Postconditions**
A critical ticket exists and a delivery record exists for each targeted staff member.

---

## UC-03 — Receive and acknowledge a critical alert

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff (recipients, other devices) |
| **Trigger** | System dispatches a critical alert (from UC-02). |
| **Preconditions** | Recipient is authenticated and registered to the same trip. |

**Main flow**
1. Recipient's device shows the **CRITICAL ALERT** card with the delegate, coach, last-seen note and departure countdown (Screen 11).
2. Recipient taps **Acknowledge** (I've seen it) or **I'm on it** (I'm actively responding).
3. System updates that recipient's `exception_alert` row (`ack_status = ACKNOWLEDGED` or `ON_IT`, with timestamp).
4. All staff/admin see live acknowledgement state so effort isn't duplicated.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A3a — Ticket resolved before acknowledgement:** the alert card auto-updates to "Resolved by <staff>" and the action buttons disable.
- **A3b — Offline recipient:** acknowledgement is queued locally and synced on reconnect.

**Postconditions**
Acknowledgement state is recorded and visible team-wide.

---

## UC-04 — Resolve or update a ticket

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff or Administrator |
| **Trigger** | The underlying issue is fixed (missing person found, badge reissued) or the ticket needs a priority/note change. |
| **Preconditions** | The ticket exists and is not already `RESOLVED` or `CANCELLED`. |

**Main flow**
1. User opens the ticket from the inbox (Screen 5) or the alert card.
2. User either edits fields (priority, note, linked delegate) **or** taps **Resolve**.
3. System applies the change; on resolve it sets `status = RESOLVED`, `resolved_at`, `resolved_by`.
4. Any active alerts for the ticket are closed and all devices update in real time.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A4a — Concurrent resolution (race):** two staff resolve the same ticket at once. System accepts the first write and returns `409 ALREADY_RESOLVED` to the second, then refreshes their view — no double state.
- **A4b — Reopen:** an admin can move a wrongly-resolved ticket back to `OPEN` (audited).

**Postconditions**
Ticket state is updated, timestamped, attributed to a user, and reflected everywhere.

---

## UC-05 — Manual attendance override when digital identification fails

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | A delegate's phone is dead, badge is lost, or facial recognition fails, but the delegate is physically present. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; the delegate exists on the trip roster. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff switches the scanner to **Manual** mode (Screen 9).
2. Staff selects the delegate and sets status to **Present**.
3. Staff provides a **reason** (e.g. "Phone dead").
4. System records the override (attributed to the staff member) and the headcount updates.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A5a — Offline queue-and-sync:** with no roaming data, the override is saved locally, the headcount updates optimistically, and the record syncs in the background on reconnect (idempotent by `clientRef`). *This is the client's core "faster than manual headcount, works overseas" requirement in action.*
- **A5b — Override conflicts with a later real scan:** if a genuine scan arrives afterwards, the scan is authoritative and the override is retained as an audit note.

**Postconditions**
Attendance is accurate, and an auditable override record exists (who, when, why).

---

## UC-06 — QR-code fallback check-in

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | Face recognition is unavailable or failing, so staff switches to **QR** on the scanner. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; delegate presents a QR badge; a trip is active. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff selects **QR** mode and holds the delegate's badge inside the frame (Screen 9).
2. The app decodes the QR payload client-side.
3. The app submits the payload to the shared check-in contract (`POST /api/attendance/scan`, owned by Vimal).
4. On success the delegate is marked present and the headcount updates.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A6a — QR unreadable / damaged:** decoding fails. The app surfaces **Can't scan? → Log exception** (routes to UC-01) or **Manual** (routes to UC-05).
- **A6b — Delegate not recognised (`404 SCAN_FAILED`):** the app prompts the same fallback choices rather than failing silently.
- **A6c — Offline:** the decoded check-in is queued and synced on reconnect.

**Postconditions**
Either the delegate is checked in, or a fallback (exception/manual) path is invoked — never a dead end.

---

## UC-07 — Monitor and triage the Exception Inbox

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | Administrator |
| **Trigger** | Admin opens the **Exception Inbox** (Screen 5) to oversee on-ground issues. |
| **Preconditions** | Admin is authenticated. |

**Main flow**
1. Admin opens the inbox and sees the summary counts (**All / Critical / Open / Resolved**).
2. Admin filters by tab or by trip/coach.
3. Admin reads ticket detail (priority, issue, delegate, coach, who raised it, time).
4. Admin resolves, reassigns priority, or opens the ticket for follow-up (→ UC-04).

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A7a — Empty state:** no active tickets → inbox shows an "all clear" state.
- **A7b — Live update:** a new critical ticket arrives while viewing → the banner and list update without a manual refresh.

**Postconditions**
Admin has an accurate, real-time view of all on-ground issues.

---

## UC-08 — Cancel / soft-delete a mistaken ticket

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff or Administrator |
| **Trigger** | A ticket was raised in error (wrong delegate, accidental submission). |
| **Preconditions** | The ticket exists. |

**Main flow**
1. User opens the ticket and selects **Cancel ticket**.
2. System sets `status = CANCELLED` and stamps `deleted_at` (soft delete — the row is retained for audit).
3. The ticket leaves the active views but remains in the audit history and export.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A8a — Attempt to cancel a resolved ticket:** allowed, but the resolution record is preserved.
- **A8b — Non-owner cancel:** permitted for admins and the original raiser; other staff are blocked (`403 FORBIDDEN`).

**Postconditions**
The ticket is removed from active workflow without destroying the audit trail (satisfies the "soft delete" allowance in the assignment brief).

---

## 2. Traceability — use cases to endpoints

| Use case | Primary endpoint(s) | CRUD / capability |
|----------|--------------------|-------------------|
| UC-01 Log exception | `POST /api/exceptions` | Create |
| UC-02 Critical alert | `POST /api/exceptions` (+ real-time channel) | Create + Enhanced (alerting) |
| UC-03 Acknowledge alert | `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/ack` | Update |
| UC-04 Resolve / update | `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id`, `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/resolve` | Update |
| UC-05 Manual override | `PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override` | Enhanced (override) |
| UC-06 QR fallback | shared `POST /api/attendance/scan` (Vimal) → fallback to UC-01/UC-05 | Enhanced (QR) |
| UC-07 Inbox monitor | `GET /api/exceptions`, `GET /api/exceptions/active` | Read |
| UC-08 Cancel ticket | `DELETE /api/exceptions/:id` (soft) | Delete |

{"language": "markdown", "code": "# Use Cases — Exception Logging, QR Fallback & Manual Override

**Module:** Full Stack Application Development (2026S1)
**Project:** SCCCI Delegation Attendance System ("MusterGo")
**Author:** Jayden
**Feature area:** Exception & Issue Logging (Support Tickets CRUD) · QR-code fallback identification · Real-time critical alerting · Manual attendance override
**Rubric mapping:** A1 System Design & Architecture (Individual)

---

## 1. Scope & Ownership

This document defines the use cases for the feature set I own. It covers three user roles and the system itself as an actor (for automated alert fan-out).

| Actor | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **On-site Staff** | Mobile-app user on the ground (lobby, coach, venue). Logs exceptions, scans QR as a fallback, performs manual overrides, receives and acknowledges alerts. |
| **Administrator** | Web-dashboard user. Monitors and triages the Exception Inbox, resolves/cancels tickets, watches critical alerts. |
| **System** | The application itself. Automatically fans out critical alerts to all staff devices and queues offline actions for later sync. |

**Integration boundary (noted for the assessor):** the shared check-in write path (`POST /api/attendance/scan`, accepting face-hash *or* QR payload) is owned by Vimal. My QR capability is the *fallback client flow* that consumes that shared contract and, on failure, routes into my exception-logging and manual-override paths. Endpoints I own are listed in `api-documentation.md`.

**Enumerations referenced below** (defined fully in `database-schema.md`):
- `issue_type`: `MISSING_PERSON`, `LOST_BADGE`, `FACE_MATCH_FAILED`, `DEAD_PHONE`, `VIP_REQUEST`, `OTHER`
- `priority`: `CRITICAL`, `NORMAL`, `LOW`
- `status`: `OPEN`, `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED`
- `ack_status`: `PENDING`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `ON_IT`

---

## UC-01 — Log an on-ground exception

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | A delegate cannot check in normally (lost badge, dead phone, face-match failure, VIP need) and staff taps **Log exception** on the mobile app. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; a trip is active; staff has the delegate in view or knows their identity. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff opens the **Log exception** screen (Screen 10).
2. Staff selects an **issue type** (e.g. *Lost badge*).
3. Staff selects the affected **delegate** from the trip roster (or leaves it blank for an unidentified person).
4. Staff adds an optional **quick note** (e.g. "Phone unreachable, last seen near gift shop 14:08").
5. Staff leaves **Mark as critical** off for a normal-priority issue and taps **Submit**.
6. System creates the ticket with `status = OPEN`, `priority = NORMAL`, returns the new `issueId`, and the ticket appears in the admin **Exception Inbox** (Screen 5).

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A1a — Offline:** device has no roaming data. System saves the ticket to a local queue, shows an "offline — will sync" indicator, and submits automatically once connectivity returns (idempotent by client-generated `clientRef`).
- **A1b — Missing required field:** no issue type selected. System blocks submission and shows an inline validation error (maps to `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`).
- **A1c — Unidentified person:** no delegate chosen. Ticket is created with `delegate_id = null` and a free-text description; can be linked to a delegate later.

**Postconditions**
A support ticket exists, is visible to all staff/admin, and is queryable in the inbox.

---

## UC-02 — Raise a critical missing-person alert (real-time fan-out)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff (raises) · System (dispatches) |
| **Trigger** | Staff logs an exception with **Mark as critical** enabled — typically a *missing person* before an imminent departure. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; a trip is active; at least one other staff device is registered to the trip. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff selects issue type **Missing person**, chooses the delegate (e.g. *Lim Wei Jie · Coach 2 · VIP*), and enables **Mark as critical — alerts all staff devices instantly**.
2. Staff taps **Submit & alert team**.
3. System creates the ticket with `priority = CRITICAL`, `status = OPEN`.
4. System fans out a **critical alert** to every registered staff device on the trip (Screen 11), creating one `exception_alert` row per recipient with `ack_status = PENDING`.
5. The admin dashboard banner updates instantly ("1 critical exception · pushed to all N staff devices").

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A2a — No recipients online:** alerts are queued and delivered on reconnect; the raiser still sees "sent, awaiting delivery".
- **A2b — Duplicate critical for same delegate:** system detects an existing `OPEN` critical ticket for that delegate on that trip and appends to it rather than creating a duplicate (prevents alert spam).
- **A2c — Delegate already resolved elsewhere:** if the delegate was checked in on another device moments earlier, the alert still sends but is flagged "possible false alarm — last seen boarded 14:09" so staff can stand down quickly.

**Postconditions**
A critical ticket exists and a delivery record exists for each targeted staff member.

---

## UC-03 — Receive and acknowledge a critical alert

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff (recipients, other devices) |
| **Trigger** | System dispatches a critical alert (from UC-02). |
| **Preconditions** | Recipient is authenticated and registered to the same trip. |

**Main flow**
1. Recipient's device shows the **CRITICAL ALERT** card with the delegate, coach, last-seen note and departure countdown (Screen 11).
2. Recipient taps **Acknowledge** (I've seen it) or **I'm on it** (I'm actively responding).
3. System updates that recipient's `exception_alert` row (`ack_status = ACKNOWLEDGED` or `ON_IT`, with timestamp).
4. All staff/admin see live acknowledgement state so effort isn't duplicated.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A3a — Ticket resolved before acknowledgement:** the alert card auto-updates to "Resolved by <staff>" and the action buttons disable.
- **A3b — Offline recipient:** acknowledgement is queued locally and synced on reconnect.

**Postconditions**
Acknowledgement state is recorded and visible team-wide.

---

## UC-04 — Resolve or update a ticket

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff or Administrator |
| **Trigger** | The underlying issue is fixed (missing person found, badge reissued) or the ticket needs a priority/note change. |
| **Preconditions** | The ticket exists and is not already `RESOLVED` or `CANCELLED`. |

**Main flow**
1. User opens the ticket from the inbox (Screen 5) or the alert card.
2. User either edits fields (priority, note, linked delegate) **or** taps **Resolve**.
3. System applies the change; on resolve it sets `status = RESOLVED`, `resolved_at`, `resolved_by`.
4. Any active alerts for the ticket are closed and all devices update in real time.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A4a — Concurrent resolution (race):** two staff resolve the same ticket at once. System accepts the first write and returns `409 ALREADY_RESOLVED` to the second, then refreshes their view — no double state.
- **A4b — Reopen:** an admin can move a wrongly-resolved ticket back to `OPEN` (audited).

**Postconditions**
Ticket state is updated, timestamped, attributed to a user, and reflected everywhere.

---

## UC-05 — Manual attendance override when digital identification fails

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | A delegate's phone is dead, badge is lost, or facial recognition fails, but the delegate is physically present. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; the delegate exists on the trip roster. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff switches the scanner to **Manual** mode (Screen 9).
2. Staff selects the delegate and sets status to **Present**.
3. Staff provides a **reason** (e.g. "Phone dead").
4. System records the override (attributed to the staff member) and the headcount updates.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A5a — Offline queue-and-sync:** with no roaming data, the override is saved locally, the headcount updates optimistically, and the record syncs in the background on reconnect (idempotent by `clientRef`). *This is the client's core "faster than manual headcount, works overseas" requirement in action.*
- **A5b — Override conflicts with a later real scan:** if a genuine scan arrives afterwards, the scan is authoritative and the override is retained as an audit note.

**Postconditions**
Attendance is accurate, and an auditable override record exists (who, when, why).

---

## UC-06 — QR-code fallback check-in

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff |
| **Trigger** | Face recognition is unavailable or failing, so staff switches to **QR** on the scanner. |
| **Preconditions** | Staff is authenticated; delegate presents a QR badge; a trip is active. |

**Main flow**
1. Staff selects **QR** mode and holds the delegate's badge inside the frame (Screen 9).
2. The app decodes the QR payload client-side.
3. The app submits the payload to the shared check-in contract (`POST /api/attendance/scan`, owned by Vimal).
4. On success the delegate is marked present and the headcount updates.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A6a — QR unreadable / damaged:** decoding fails. The app surfaces **Can't scan? → Log exception** (routes to UC-01) or **Manual** (routes to UC-05).
- **A6b — Delegate not recognised (`404 SCAN_FAILED`):** the app prompts the same fallback choices rather than failing silently.
- **A6c — Offline:** the decoded check-in is queued and synced on reconnect.

**Postconditions**
Either the delegate is checked in, or a fallback (exception/manual) path is invoked — never a dead end.

---

## UC-07 — Monitor and triage the Exception Inbox

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | Administrator |
| **Trigger** | Admin opens the **Exception Inbox** (Screen 5) to oversee on-ground issues. |
| **Preconditions** | Admin is authenticated. |

**Main flow**
1. Admin opens the inbox and sees the summary counts (**All / Critical / Open / Resolved**).
2. Admin filters by tab or by trip/coach.
3. Admin reads ticket detail (priority, issue, delegate, coach, who raised it, time).
4. Admin resolves, reassigns priority, or opens the ticket for follow-up (→ UC-04).

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A7a — Empty state:** no active tickets → inbox shows an "all clear" state.
- **A7b — Live update:** a new critical ticket arrives while viewing → the banner and list update without a manual refresh.

**Postconditions**
Admin has an accurate, real-time view of all on-ground issues.

---

## UC-08 — Cancel / soft-delete a mistaken ticket

| | |
|---|---|
| **Actor** | On-site Staff or Administrator |
| **Trigger** | A ticket was raised in error (wrong delegate, accidental submission). |
| **Preconditions** | The ticket exists. |

**Main flow**
1. User opens the ticket and selects **Cancel ticket**.
2. System sets `status = CANCELLED` and stamps `deleted_at` (soft delete — the row is retained for audit).
3. The ticket leaves the active views but remains in the audit history and export.

**Alternative / edge flows**
- **A8a — Attempt to cancel a resolved ticket:** allowed, but the resolution record is preserved.
- **A8b — Non-owner cancel:** permitted for admins and the original raiser; other staff are blocked (`403 FORBIDDEN`).

**Postconditions**
The ticket is removed from active workflow without destroying the audit trail (satisfies the "soft delete" allowance in the assignment brief).

---

## 2. Traceability — use cases to endpoints

| Use case | Primary endpoint(s) | CRUD / capability |
|----------|--------------------|-------------------|
| UC-01 Log exception | `POST /api/exceptions` | Create |
| UC-02 Critical alert | `POST /api/exceptions` (+ real-time channel) | Create + Enhanced (alerting) |
| UC-03 Acknowledge alert | `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/ack` | Update |
| UC-04 Resolve / update | `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id`, `PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/resolve` | Update |

input.file_text:
# API Documentation — Exceptions, Alerts, Manual Override & QR Fallback

**Author:** Jayden · **Rubric mapping:** A1 System Design & Architecture (Individual)
**Feature area:** Support-ticket CRUD, real-time critical alerting, manual attendance override, QR fallback boundary.

---

## 1. Conventions

**Base URL (production):** `https://<render-app>.onrender.com/api`
**Format:** JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) unless stated otherwise.

**Authentication:** All endpoints require a Bearer JWT obtained from the shared `POST /api/auth/login`.
```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>
```

**Roles:** `admin` (web dashboard) and `staff` (mobile). Role is embedded in the JWT and enforced by `requireAuth` + `requireRole` middleware on protected routes.

**Idempotency (offline-first):** write requests that originate on-device carry a client-generated `clientRef` (UUID). The server treats a repeated `clientRef` as the same operation, so queued offline actions can safely retry on reconnect without creating duplicates.

**Standard error shape:**
```json
{ "error": "ERROR_CODE", "message": "Human-readable explanation" }
```

**Common error codes (may be returned by any endpoint):**

| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | Malformed request. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing or invalid JWT. |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Authenticated but not allowed for this role/resource. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | State conflict (e.g. already resolved). |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Body failed validation; `details` lists offending fields. |
| 500 | `SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected server error. |

---

## 2. Owned endpoints

### 2.1 Create an exception ticket

`POST /api/exceptions` — **Role:** `staff`, `admin`

Creates a support ticket. Setting `markCritical: true` triggers real-time fan-out to all staff devices on the trip (see §3).

**Request**
```json
{
  "clientRef": "b3f1c2a4-...-9e",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "coachId": "coach-2",
  "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
  "note": "Phone unreachable. Last seen near gift shop at 14:08.",
  "markCritical": true
}
```
`delegateId` and `coachId` are optional (nullable for an unidentified person). `issueType` must be one of the defined enum values.

**Response — 201 Created**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "status": "OPEN",
  "priority": "CRITICAL",
  "alertDispatched": true,
  "recipients": 5,
  "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Missing `issueType`, or invalid enum value. |
| 404 | `TRIP_NOT_FOUND` | `tripId` does not exist. |
| 409 | `DUPLICATE_CRITICAL` | An open critical ticket already exists for this delegate on this trip (returns the existing `issueId`). |

---

### 2.2 List exception tickets

`GET /api/exceptions` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

Powers the Exception Inbox (Screen 5). Supports filtering and pagination.

**Query parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `tripId` | string | Filter to one trip. |
| `status` | enum | `OPEN` \| `RESOLVED` \| `CANCELLED`. |
| `priority` | enum | `CRITICAL` \| `NORMAL` \| `LOW`. |
| `coachId` | string | Filter to one coach. |
| `page`, `limit` | int | Pagination (default `page=1`, `limit=20`). |

**Example:** `GET /api/exceptions?tripId=trip-123&status=OPEN&priority=CRITICAL`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "count": 8,
  "summary": { "all": 8, "critical": 1, "open": 3, "resolved": 4 },
  "items": [
    {
      "issueId": "err-999",
      "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
      "priority": "CRITICAL",
      "status": "OPEN",
      "delegate": { "id": "del-001", "name": "Lim Wei Jie", "coach": "Coach 2" },
      "raisedBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
      "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### 2.3 Read active tickets (cross-device sync)

`GET /api/exceptions/active` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

Returns all unresolved (`OPEN`) tickets for a trip. Used by staff devices to stay in sync and to render alert badges.

**Example:** `GET /api/exceptions/active?tripId=trip-123`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "activeCount": 3,
  "items": [ { "issueId": "err-999", "priority": "CRITICAL", "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON" } ]
}
```

---

### 2.4 Read a single ticket

`GET /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
  "priority": "CRITICAL",
  "status": "OPEN",
  "note": "Phone unreachable. Last seen near gift shop at 14:08.",
  "delegate": { "id": "del-001", "name": "Lim Wei Jie" },
  "raisedBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
  "alerts": [
    { "recipientId": "usr-02", "ackStatus": "ON_IT", "acknowledgedAt": "2026-07-02T14:19:10Z" }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
}
```

**Errors:** `404 NOT_FOUND` if the ticket does not exist.

---

### 2.5 Update a ticket

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff` (raiser)

Partial update of mutable fields (`priority`, `note`, `delegateId`, `coachId`). Cannot mutate a `RESOLVED`/`CANCELLED` ticket except by an admin reopen.

**Request**
```json
{ "priority": "NORMAL", "note": "Delegate located, escorting back to coach." }
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "priority": "NORMAL", "updatedAt": "2026-07-02T14:22:00Z" }
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Non-admin, non-raiser attempts to edit. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | Ticket is already resolved/cancelled. |

---

### 2.6 Resolve a ticket

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/resolve` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

**Request**
```json
{ "resolutionNote": "Missing person found at gift shop, boarded 14:25." }
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "status": "RESOLVED",
  "resolvedBy": { "id": "usr-02", "name": "Su Lin" },
  "resolvedAt": "2026-07-02T14:25:00Z"
}
```

**Errors:** `409 ALREADY_RESOLVED` if another user resolved it first (concurrency guard — UC-04 A4a).

---

### 2.7 Acknowledge a critical alert

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/ack` — **Role:** `staff`, `admin`

Records the calling user's response to a critical alert (Screen 11).

**Request**
```json
{ "ackStatus": "ON_IT" }
```
`ackStatus` ∈ `ACKNOWLEDGED` \| `ON_IT`.

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "recipientId": "usr-02", "ackStatus": "ON_IT", "acknowledgedAt": "2026-07-02T14:19:10Z" }
```

**Errors:** `404 ALERT_NOT_FOUND` if the caller was not a recipient of this alert.

---

### 2.8 Cancel / soft-delete a ticket

`DELETE /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff` (raiser)

Soft delete. Sets `status = CANCELLED` and stamps `deleted_at`; the row is retained for audit and export.

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "status": "CANCELLED", "deletedAt": "2026-07-02T14:30:00Z" }
```

**Errors:** `403 FORBIDDEN` for a non-owner, non-admin caller.

---

### 2.9 Manual attendance override

`PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override` — **Role:** `staff`

Enhanced capability. Records a manual present/absent decision when digital identification fails, with a mandatory reason and full attribution. Offline-safe via `clientRef`.

**Request**
```json
{
  "clientRef": "8ac0...-11",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "coachId": "coach-2",
  "manualStatus": "PRESENT",
  "reason": "Phone dead"
}
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "manualStatus": "PRESENT",
  "overriddenBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
  "synced": true,
  "recordedAt": "2026-07-02T14:20:00Z"
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Missing `manualStatus` or `reason`. |
| 404 | `DELEGATE_NOT_FOUND` | `delegateId` not on this trip. |

---

## 3. Real-time critical-alert channel (Enhanced capability)

Critical tickets are pushed to staff devices over a persistent connection rather than polling.

**Transport:** WebSocket (`wss://<render-app>.onrender.com/ws`), with Server-Sent Events (`GET /api/exceptions/stream?tripId=...`) as a firewall-friendly fallback — relevant to the "must work behind the China Firewall" requirement.

**Handshake:** the client connects with its JWT and subscribes to its active `tripId`.

**Server → client events**
| Event | Payload | Meaning |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `exception:critical` | `{ issueId, delegate, coachId, note, departureInMin }` | A new critical ticket was raised (renders the Screen 11 alert card). |
| `exception:updated` | `{ issueId, status }` | Ticket changed (e.g. resolved) — cards update/close live. |
| `alert:ack` | `{ issueId, recipientId, ackStatus }` | Another staff member acknowledged / is on it. |

**Delivery guarantee:** for each critical ticket the server writes one `exception_alert` row per recipient (`PENDING`). Recipients offline at send time receive the alert on reconnect (at-least-once; the client de-duplicates by `issueId`).

---

## 4. Referenced endpoint (owned by a teammate)

Documented here only to make my QR fallback boundary explicit — **not** implemented by me.

`POST /api/attendance/scan` — **Owner:** Vimal. Accepts a face-hash **or** QR payload and writes the check-in. My QR scanner (Screen 9) decodes the badge client-side and calls this endpoint; on `404 SCAN_FAILED` or a decode failure, my client routes the staff member to `POST /api/exceptions` (UC-01) or `PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override` (UC-05).

---

## 5. Endpoint summary

| # | Method | Path | CRUD / capability | Role |
|---|--------|------|-------------------|------|
| 1 | POST | `/api/exceptions` | Create (+ alert) | staff, admin |
| 2 | GET | `/api/exceptions` | Read (list) | staff, admin |
| 3 | GET | `/api/exceptions/active` | Read (sync) | staff, admin |
| 4 | GET | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Read (single) | staff, admin |

{"language": "markdown", "code": "# API Documentation — Exceptions, Alerts, Manual Override & QR Fallback

**Author:** Jayden · **Rubric mapping:** A1 System Design & Architecture (Individual)
**Feature area:** Support-ticket CRUD, real-time critical alerting, manual attendance override, QR fallback boundary.

---

## 1. Conventions

**Base URL (production):** `https://<render-app>.onrender.com/api`
**Format:** JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) unless stated otherwise.

**Authentication:** All endpoints require a Bearer JWT obtained from the shared `POST /api/auth/login`.
```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>
```

**Roles:** `admin` (web dashboard) and `staff` (mobile). Role is embedded in the JWT and enforced by `requireAuth` + `requireRole` middleware on protected routes.

**Idempotency (offline-first):** write requests that originate on-device carry a client-generated `clientRef` (UUID). The server treats a repeated `clientRef` as the same operation, so queued offline actions can safely retry on reconnect without creating duplicates.

**Standard error shape:**
```json
{ "error": "ERROR_CODE", "message": "Human-readable explanation" }
```

**Common error codes (may be returned by any endpoint):**

| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | Malformed request. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing or invalid JWT. |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Authenticated but not allowed for this role/resource. |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | State conflict (e.g. already resolved). |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Body failed validation; `details` lists offending fields. |
| 500 | `SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected server error. |

---

## 2. Owned endpoints

### 2.1 Create an exception ticket

`POST /api/exceptions` — **Role:** `staff`, `admin`

Creates a support ticket. Setting `markCritical: true` triggers real-time fan-out to all staff devices on the trip (see §3).

**Request**
```json
{
  "clientRef": "b3f1c2a4-...-9e",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "coachId": "coach-2",
  "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
  "note": "Phone unreachable. Last seen near gift shop at 14:08.",
  "markCritical": true
}
```
`delegateId` and `coachId` are optional (nullable for an unidentified person). `issueType` must be one of the defined enum values.

**Response — 201 Created**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "status": "OPEN",
  "priority": "CRITICAL",
  "alertDispatched": true,
  "recipients": 5,
  "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Missing `issueType`, or invalid enum value. |
| 404 | `TRIP_NOT_FOUND` | `tripId` does not exist. |
| 409 | `DUPLICATE_CRITICAL` | An open critical ticket already exists for this delegate on this trip (returns the existing `issueId`). |

---

### 2.2 List exception tickets

`GET /api/exceptions` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

Powers the Exception Inbox (Screen 5). Supports filtering and pagination.

**Query parameters**
| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `tripId` | string | Filter to one trip. |
| `status` | enum | `OPEN` \| `RESOLVED` \| `CANCELLED`. |
| `priority` | enum | `CRITICAL` \| `NORMAL` \| `LOW`. |
| `coachId` | string | Filter to one coach. |
| `page`, `limit` | int | Pagination (default `page=1`, `limit=20`). |

**Example:** `GET /api/exceptions?tripId=trip-123&status=OPEN&priority=CRITICAL`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "count": 8,
  "summary": { "all": 8, "critical": 1, "open": 3, "resolved": 4 },
  "items": [
    {
      "issueId": "err-999",
      "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
      "priority": "CRITICAL",
      "status": "OPEN",
      "delegate": { "id": "del-001", "name": "Lim Wei Jie", "coach": "Coach 2" },
      "raisedBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
      "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### 2.3 Read active tickets (cross-device sync)

`GET /api/exceptions/active` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

Returns all unresolved (`OPEN`) tickets for a trip. Used by staff devices to stay in sync and to render alert badges.

**Example:** `GET /api/exceptions/active?tripId=trip-123`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "activeCount": 3,
  "items": [ { "issueId": "err-999", "priority": "CRITICAL", "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON" } ]
}
```

---

### 2.4 Read a single ticket

`GET /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "issueType": "MISSING_PERSON",
  "priority": "CRITICAL",
  "status": "OPEN",
  "note": "Phone unreachable. Last seen near gift shop at 14:08.",
  "delegate": { "id": "del-001", "name": "Lim Wei Jie" },
  "raisedBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
  "alerts": [
    { "recipientId": "usr-02", "ackStatus": "ON_IT", "acknowledgedAt": "2026-07-02T14:19:10Z" }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2026-07-02T14:18:00Z"
}
```

**Errors:** `404 NOT_FOUND` if the ticket does not exist.

---

### 2.5 Update a ticket

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff` (raiser)

Partial update of mutable fields (`priority`, `note`, `delegateId`, `coachId`). Cannot mutate a `RESOLVED`/`CANCELLED` ticket except by an admin reopen.

**Request**
```json
{ "priority": "NORMAL", "note": "Delegate located, escorting back to coach." }
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "priority": "NORMAL", "updatedAt": "2026-07-02T14:22:00Z" }
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Non-admin, non-raiser attempts to edit. |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | Ticket is already resolved/cancelled. |

---

### 2.6 Resolve a ticket

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/resolve` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff`

**Request**
```json
{ "resolutionNote": "Missing person found at gift shop, boarded 14:25." }
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "issueId": "err-999",
  "status": "RESOLVED",
  "resolvedBy": { "id": "usr-02", "name": "Su Lin" },
  "resolvedAt": "2026-07-02T14:25:00Z"
}
```

**Errors:** `409 ALREADY_RESOLVED` if another user resolved it first (concurrency guard — UC-04 A4a).

---

### 2.7 Acknowledge a critical alert

`PATCH /api/exceptions/:id/ack` — **Role:** `staff`, `admin`

Records the calling user's response to a critical alert (Screen 11).

**Request**
```json
{ "ackStatus": "ON_IT" }
```
`ackStatus` ∈ `ACKNOWLEDGED` \| `ON_IT`.

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "recipientId": "usr-02", "ackStatus": "ON_IT", "acknowledgedAt": "2026-07-02T14:19:10Z" }
```

**Errors:** `404 ALERT_NOT_FOUND` if the caller was not a recipient of this alert.

---

### 2.8 Cancel / soft-delete a ticket

`DELETE /api/exceptions/:id` — **Role:** `admin`, `staff` (raiser)

Soft delete. Sets `status = CANCELLED` and stamps `deleted_at`; the row is retained for audit and export.

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{ "issueId": "err-999", "status": "CANCELLED", "deletedAt": "2026-07-02T14:30:00Z" }
```

**Errors:** `403 FORBIDDEN` for a non-owner, non-admin caller.

---

### 2.9 Manual attendance override

`PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override` — **Role:** `staff`

Enhanced capability. Records a manual present/absent decision when digital identification fails, with a mandatory reason and full attribution. Offline-safe via `clientRef`.

**Request**
```json
{
  "clientRef": "8ac0...-11",
  "tripId": "trip-123",
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "coachId": "coach-2",
  "manualStatus": "PRESENT",
  "reason": "Phone dead"
}
```

**Response — 200 OK**
```json
{
  "delegateId": "del-001",
  "manualStatus": "PRESENT",
  "overriddenBy": { "id": "usr-07", "name": "Wei Ming" },
  "synced": true,
  "recordedAt": "2026-07-02T14:20:00Z"
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Missing `manualStatus` or `reason`. |
| 404 | `DELEGATE_NOT_FOUND` | `delegateId` not on this trip. |

---

## 3. Real-time critical-alert channel (Enhanced capability)

Critical tickets are pushed to staff devices over a persistent connection rather than polling.

**Transport:** WebSocket (`wss://<render-app>.onrender.com/ws`), with Server-Sent Events (`GET /api/exceptions/stream?tripId=...`) as a firewall-friendly fallback — relevant to the "must work behind the China Firewall" requirement.

**Handshake:** the client connects with its JWT and subscribes to its active `tripId`.

**Server → client events**
| Event | Payload | Meaning |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `exception:critical` | `{ issueId, delegate, coachId, note, departureInMin }` | A new critical ticket was raised (renders the Screen 11 alert card). |
| `exception:updated` | `{ issueId, status }` | Ticket changed (e.g. resolved) — cards update/close live. |
| `alert:ack` | `{ issueId, recipientId, ackStatus }` | Another staff member acknowledged / is on it. |

**Delivery guarantee:** for each critical ticket the server writes one `exception_alert` row per recipient (`PENDING`). Recipients offline at send time receive the alert on reconnect (at-least-once; the client de-duplicates by `issueId`).

---

## 4. Referenced endpoint (owned by a teammate)

Documented here only to make my QR fallback boundary explicit — **not** implemented by me.

`POST /api/attendance/scan` — **Owner:** Vimal. Accepts a face-hash **or** QR payload and writes the check-in. My QR scanner (Screen 9) decodes the badge client-side and calls this endpoint; on `404 SCAN_FAILED` or a decode failure, my client routes the staff member to `POST /api/exceptions` (UC-01) or `PATCH /api/attendance/manual-override` (UC-05).

---

## 5. Endpoint summary

| # | Method | Path | CRUD / capability | Role |
|---|--------|------|-------------------|------|
| 1 | POST | `/api/exceptions` | Create (+ alert) | staff, admin |
| 2 | GET | `/api/exceptions` | Read (list) | staff, admin |
| 3 | GET | `/api/exceptions/active` | Read (sync) | staff, admin |
| 4 | GET | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Read (single) | staff, admin |
| 5 | PATCH | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Update | admin, raiser |
| 6 | PATCH | `/api/exceptions/:id/resolve` | Update (resolve) | staff, admin |
| 7 | PATCH | `/api/exceptions/:id/ack` | Update (acknowledge) | staff, admin |
| 8 | DELETE | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Delete (soft) | admin, raiser |
| 9 | PATCH | `/api/attendance/manual-override` | Enhanced (override) | staff |
| — | WS/SSE | `/ws`, `/api/exceptions/stream` | Enhanced (real-time alert) | staff, admin |
", "filename": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/docs/jayden/api-documentation.md"}

# Database Schema — Exceptions, Alerts & Manual Override

**Author:** Jayden · **Rubric mapping:** A1 System Design & Architecture (Individual)
**Scope:** Tables I own (`exceptions`, `exception_alerts`, `attendance_overrides`) plus the teammate-owned tables they relate to, shown for relationship context.

> The diagram below is written in Mermaid. It renders on GitHub and in VS Code (Markdown Preview Mermaid Support extension). For the group submission, export it as `docs/architecture-diagram.png` if a static image is preferred.

---

## 1. Entity-Relationship Diagram

```mermaid
erDiagram
    TRIPS ||--o{ EXCEPTIONS : "has"
    TRIPS ||--o{ ATTENDANCE_OVERRIDES : "has"
    DELEGATES ||--o{ EXCEPTIONS : "subject of"
    DELEGATES ||--o{ ATTENDANCE_OVERRIDES : "subject of"
    COACHES ||--o{ EXCEPTIONS : "located at"
    USERS ||--o{ EXCEPTIONS : "raises"
    USERS ||--o{ EXCEPTIONS : "resolves"
    USERS ||--o{ ATTENDANCE_OVERRIDES : "overrides"
    EXCEPTIONS ||--o{ EXCEPTION_ALERTS : "fans out to"
    USERS ||--o{ EXCEPTION_ALERTS : "receives"

    EXCEPTIONS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid trip_id FK
        uuid delegate_id FK "nullable"
        uuid coach_id FK "nullable"
        enum issue_type
        enum priority
        enum status
        boolean is_critical
        text note
        uuid raised_by FK
        uuid resolved_by FK "nullable"
        text resolution_note "nullable"
        uuid client_ref "unique, offline idempotency"
        timestamptz created_at
        timestamptz resolved_at "nullable"
        timestamptz deleted_at "nullable, soft delete"
    }

    EXCEPTION_ALERTS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid exception_id FK
        uuid recipient_id FK
        enum ack_status
        timestamptz delivered_at "nullable"
        timestamptz acknowledged_at "nullable"
        timestamptz created_at
    }

    ATTENDANCE_OVERRIDES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid trip_id FK
        uuid delegate_id FK
        uuid coach_id FK "nullable"
        enum manual_status
        text reason
        uuid overridden_by FK
        uuid client_ref "unique, offline idempotency"
        boolean synced
        timestamptz created_at
    }

    TRIPS {
        uuid id PK
        string trip_name
        date start_date
        date end_date
    }
    DELEGATES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid trip_id FK
        string name
        string coach_id
    }
    COACHES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid trip_id FK
        string label
        int capacity
    }
    USERS {
        uuid id PK
        string name
        enum role
    }
```

---

## 2. Owned tables

### 2.1 `exceptions`

The core support-ticket entity (maps to the assignment's "Support Tickets" CRUD).

| Column | Type | Key / Constraint | Notes |
|--------|------|------------------|-------|
| `id` | UUID | PK | Generated server-side. |
| `trip_id` | UUID | FK → `trips.id`, NOT NULL | The trip the ticket belongs to. |
| `delegate_id` | UUID | FK → `delegates.id`, NULL | Nullable — an exception may concern an unidentified person. |
| `coach_id` | UUID | FK → `coaches.id`, NULL | Where the issue occurred. |
| `issue_type` | ENUM `issue_type` | NOT NULL | See §4. |
| `priority` | ENUM `priority` | NOT NULL, default `NORMAL` | `CRITICAL` when raised as an alert. |
| `status` | ENUM `status` | NOT NULL, default `OPEN` | Lifecycle state. |
| `is_critical` | BOOLEAN | NOT NULL, default `false` | Denormalised flag for fast inbox filtering / banner. |
| `note` | TEXT | NULL | Free-text detail (e.g. last-seen location). |
| `raised_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Staff/admin who created the ticket. |
| `resolved_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NULL | Who resolved it. |
| `resolution_note` | TEXT | NULL | How it was resolved. |
| `client_ref` | UUID | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | Client-generated; enforces offline idempotency. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |
| `resolved_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set on resolve. |
| `deleted_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Soft-delete marker (ticket cancelled). |

**Indexes:** `(trip_id, status)`, `(trip_id, priority)`, `(delegate_id)`, unique `(client_ref)`.

---

### 2.2 `exception_alerts`

One row per recipient of a critical alert — models the "pushed to all N staff devices" fan-out and per-device acknowledgement (Screen 11). Normalising this into its own table (rather than a column on `exceptions`) keeps the design scalable: an alert can reach any number of staff without altering the ticket row.

| Column | Type | Key / Constraint | Notes |
|--------|------|------------------|-------|
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `exception_id` | UUID | FK → `exceptions.id`, NOT NULL | The ticket that triggered the alert. |
| `recipient_id` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Targeted staff member. |
| `ack_status` | ENUM `ack_status` | NOT NULL, default `PENDING` | `PENDING` \| `ACKNOWLEDGED` \| `ON_IT`. |
| `delivered_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set when the device confirms receipt. |
| `acknowledged_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set on Acknowledge / I'm on it. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |

**Constraints:** UNIQUE `(exception_id, recipient_id)` — a recipient is alerted once per ticket.
**Indexes:** `(recipient_id, ack_status)`.

---

### 2.3 `attendance_overrides`

Audit trail for manual overrides (enhanced capability). Kept separate from the shared `attendance` table (Vimal's) so my feature owns its own auditable record — who overrode, why, and whether the offline entry has synced.

| Column | Type | Key / Constraint | Notes |
|--------|------|------------------|-------|
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `trip_id` | UUID | FK → `trips.id`, NOT NULL | |
| `delegate_id` | UUID | FK → `delegates.id`, NOT NULL | |
| `coach_id` | UUID | FK → `coaches.id`, NULL | |
| `manual_status` | ENUM `manual_status` | NOT NULL | `PRESENT` \| `ABSENT`. |
| `reason` | TEXT | NOT NULL | Mandatory (e.g. "Phone dead"). |
| `overridden_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Staff member. |
| `client_ref` | UUID | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | Offline idempotency. |
| `synced` | BOOLEAN | NOT NULL, default `true` | `false` while queued offline. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |

**Indexes:** `(trip_id, delegate_id)`, unique `(client_ref)`.

---

## 3. Referenced tables (owned by teammates)

Shown only to make foreign-key relationships explicit; full definitions live in the respective owners' schema docs.

| Table | Owner | Columns used here |
|-------|-------|-------------------|
| `trips` | Desmond | `id` |
| `delegates` | Vance | `id`, `trip_id`, `name` |
| `coaches` | Desmond | `id`, `trip_id`, `label`, `capacity` |
| `users` | Shared (auth) | `id`, `name`, `role` |
| `attendance` | Vimal | check-in records the QR/manual paths ultimately affect |

---

## 4. Enumerations

| Enum | Values |
|------|--------|
| `issue_type` | `MISSING_PERSON`, `LOST_BADGE`, `FACE_MATCH_FAILED`, `DEAD_PHONE`, `VIP_REQUEST`, `OTHER` |
| `priority` | `CRITICAL`, `NORMAL`, `LOW` |
| `status` | `OPEN`, `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `ack_status` | `PENDING`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `ON_IT` |
| `manual_status` | `PRESENT`, `ABSENT` |

---

## 5. Normalisation notes

- **1NF:** every column holds a single atomic value; there are no repeating groups. Multiple alert recipients are represented as multiple `exception_alerts` rows, not a comma-separated list.
- **2NF:** all non-key attributes depend on the whole primary key. Each table has a single-column UUID PK, so there are no partial-key dependencies.
- **3NF:** no transitive dependencies. Delegate name, coach label, and user name are **not** duplicated into `exceptions`; they are reached by foreign key. The one deliberate denormalisation is `is_critical`, a cached flag mirroring `priority = CRITICAL` purely to speed up the inbox banner query — a documented, controlled exception.
- **Referential integrity:** foreign keys use `ON DELETE RESTRICT` for trips/delegates (you cannot delete a trip with live tickets) and soft deletes (`deleted_at`) for tickets, so history is never physically lost — supporting the post-trip CSV/Excel export the client requires.
- **Scalability:** the alert fan-out table grows linearly with (tickets × staff) and is indexed on `(recipient_id, ack_status)` so a device's "my pending alerts" query stays fast as trips scale to 150+ delegates and multiple coaches.

| `is_critical` | BOOLEAN | NOT NULL, default `false` | Denormalised flag for fast inbox filtering / banner. |
| `note` | TEXT | NULL | Free-text detail (e.g. last-seen location). |
| `raised_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Staff/admin who created the ticket. |
| `resolved_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NULL | Who resolved it. |
| `resolution_note` | TEXT | NULL | How it was resolved. |
| `client_ref` | UUID | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | Client-generated; enforces offline idempotency. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |
| `resolved_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set on resolve. |
| `deleted_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Soft-delete marker (ticket cancelled). |

**Indexes:** `(trip_id, status)`, `(trip_id, priority)`, `(delegate_id)`, unique `(client_ref)`.

---

### 2.2 `exception_alerts`

One row per recipient of a critical alert — models the "pushed to all N staff devices" fan-out and per-device acknowledgement (Screen 11). Normalising this into its own table (rather than a column on `exceptions`) keeps the design scalable: an alert can reach any number of staff without altering the ticket row.

| Column | Type | Key / Constraint | Notes |
|--------|------|------------------|-------|
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `exception_id` | UUID | FK → `exceptions.id`, NOT NULL | The ticket that triggered the alert. |
| `recipient_id` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Targeted staff member. |
| `ack_status` | ENUM `ack_status` | NOT NULL, default `PENDING` | `PENDING` \| `ACKNOWLEDGED` \| `ON_IT`. |
| `delivered_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set when the device confirms receipt. |
| `acknowledged_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NULL | Set on Acknowledge / I'm on it. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |

**Constraints:** UNIQUE `(exception_id, recipient_id)` — a recipient is alerted once per ticket.
**Indexes:** `(recipient_id, ack_status)`.

---

### 2.3 `attendance_overrides`

Audit trail for manual overrides (enhanced capability). Kept separate from the shared `attendance` table (Vimal's) so my feature owns its own auditable record — who overrode, why, and whether the offline entry has synced.

| Column | Type | Key / Constraint | Notes |
|--------|------|------------------|-------|
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `trip_id` | UUID | FK → `trips.id`, NOT NULL | |
| `delegate_id` | UUID | FK → `delegates.id`, NOT NULL | |
| `coach_id` | UUID | FK → `coaches.id`, NULL | |
| `manual_status` | ENUM `manual_status` | NOT NULL | `PRESENT` \| `ABSENT`. |
| `reason` | TEXT | NOT NULL | Mandatory (e.g. "Phone dead"). |
| `overridden_by` | UUID | FK → `users.id`, NOT NULL | Staff member. |
| `client_ref` | UUID | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | Offline idempotency. |
| `synced` | BOOLEAN | NOT NULL, default `true` | `false` while queued offline. |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | NOT NULL, default `now()` | |

**Indexes:** `(trip_id, delegate_id)`, unique `(client_ref)`.

---

## 3. Referenced tables (owned by teammates)

Shown only to make foreign-key relationships explicit; full definitions live in the respective owners' schema docs.

| Table | Owner | Columns used here |
|-------|-------|-------------------|
| `trips` | Desmond | `id` |
| `delegates` | Vance | `id`, `trip_id`, `name` |
| `coaches` | Desmond | `id`, `trip_id`, `label`, `capacity` |
| `users` | Shared (auth) | `id`, `name`, `role` |
| `attendance` | Vimal | check-in records the QR/manual paths ultimately affect |

---

## 4. Enumerations

| Enum | Values |
|------|--------|
| `issue_type` | `MISSING_PERSON`, `LOST_BADGE`, `FACE_MATCH_FAILED`, `DEAD_PHONE`, `VIP_REQUEST`, `OTHER` |
| `priority` | `CRITICAL`, `NORMAL`, `LOW` |
| `status` | `OPEN`, `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `ack_status` | `PENDING`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `ON_IT` |
| `manual_status` | `PRESENT`, `ABSENT` |

---

## 5. Normalisation notes

- **1NF:** every column holds a single atomic value; there are no repeating groups. Multiple alert recipients are represented as multiple `exception_alerts` rows, not a comma-separated list.
- **2NF:** all non-key attributes depend on the whole primary key. Each table has a single-column UUID PK, so there are no partial-key dependencies.
- **3NF:** no transitive dependencies. Delegate name, coach label, and user name are **not** duplicated into `exceptions`; they are reached by foreign key. The one deliberate denormalisation is `is_critical`, a cached flag mirroring `priority = CRITICAL` purely to speed up the inbox banner query — a documented, controlled exception.
- **Referential integrity:** foreign keys use `ON DELETE RESTRICT` for trips/delegates (you cannot delete a trip with live tickets) and soft deletes (`deleted_at`) for tickets, so history is never physically lost — supporting the post-trip CSV/Excel export the client requires.
- **Scalability:** the alert fan-out table grows linearly with (tickets × staff) and is indexed on `(recipient_id, ack_status)` so a device's "my pending alerts" query stays fast as trips scale to 150+ delegates and multiple coaches.

The key question is what "functional" really means here — he's asking for a page that can actually perform CRUD operations on exceptions, not just display static data. Given the tech stack (React frontend, Node backend, MySQL database), that means I need to build the complete vertical slice: the React component for the Exception Inbox page, the backend API endpoints to handle exception data, and the MySQL schema to store and query that data. He's emphasizing MySQL specifically, which signals he wants the data layer properly implemented, not mocked out. Building the backend with Express and MySQL, using a real connection pool and SQL queries, but also adding a simulation toggle (like the teammate's pattern) so the frontend works immediately without needing MySQL running — then providing a schema.sql file and seed data for when he deploys it properly. ify the frontend builds and renders with seeded data, and attempt to run MySQL in the sandbox to test the full stack—if it works, I'll screenshot the real integration; if not, I'll fall back to verifying the frontend with a running Express server. I'm structuring the deliverable as a clean project addition with a new `server/` directory containing the Node/Express backend, MySQL schema and seed files, connection pool setup, and API routes for the exceptions feature, alongside the rewritten React page and API client.

Now I'm reconsidering the scope—he asked me to focus on the exception logging page, but "functionable" plus "strictly MySQL" implies I need to build the backend and data layer too, not just the frontend. The exceptions feature should be fully functional with MySQL backing it, so the deliverable is the page plus the API that powers it, staying within the exceptions domain. I'm clarifying whether the logging page should include the create form or just the read/triage view—logging typically happens on mobile, but the admin inbox might support creating exceptions directly as well.

For CRUD coverage, I'll include Create (a modal to log exceptions), Read (list with filtering and detail view), Update (resolve, edit priority/notes), and Delete (soft cancel). That gives me full CRUD on the admin page. For the enhanced capability around real-time alerting, I'm deciding between polling and WebSocket—polling is simpler and reliable for a demo, but implementing a real WebSocket broadcast for critical alerts would be more impressive and still achievable with mysql2 and a ws library.

Actually, Server-Sent Events is the better choice here. It's lighter than WebSocket, works well across firewalls (which aligns with the China Firewall consideration mentioned in the API docs), and is straightforward to implement. The inbox will subscribe to an `/api/exceptions/stream` endpoint and receive live updates as exceptions are created or resolved. That's a clean, genuinely functional "enhanced capability" without overcomplicating the stack.

For the database schema, I need to decide on ID strategy—I could use `CHAR(36)` for app-generated UUIDs, `BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT` for simplicity, or a hybrid approach with a public string ID like "err-999" for readability in the demo.  UUID is more robust and professional, so I'll go with that. I'll also use MySQL's native ENUM columns for issue_type, priority, status, and ack_status, and DATETIME for timestamps.

The trickier decision is foreign keys. Since the exceptions module needs to reference trips, delegates, coaches, and users tables that belong to teammates, I have two options: either create minimal stub tables in my schema so the app runs standalone with proper foreign key constraints, or denormalize and store names directly on the exception record. For maintaining 3NF and demonstrating real relational design, I'll create the reference tables as minimal stubs with clear documentation that they're placeholders for local development, then seed them with sample data. This keeps the schema normalized and lets me show proper joins while still being runnable independently.

For the frontend, I need to handle responsive design carefully. On desktop the table layout works fine, but on mobile (≤720px) tables don't work well, so I'll render both a table and a card-based layout, toggling between them via CSS media queries. Each card will display the ticket's priority, issue type, delegate/coach, raised date, status, and action buttons. I'll also make sure the critical banner and filter tabs reflow properly on narrow screens, and add a modal form for logging new exceptions that works as a full-screen sheet on mobile.

content.text:
1	---
     2	name: frontend-design
     3	description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Frontend Design
     8	
     9	Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.
    10	
    11	## Ground it in the subject
    12	
    13	If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
    14	
    15	## Design principles
    16	
    17	For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.
    18	
    19	Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
    20	
    21	Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.
    22	
    23	Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.
    24	
    25	Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
    26	
    27	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
    28	
    29	## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again
    30	
    31	For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell); (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
    32	
    33	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.
    34	
    35	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.
    36	
    37	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.
    38	
    39	Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.
    40	
    41	## Restraint and self-critique
    42	
    43	Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
    44	
    45	## More on writing in design
    46	
    47	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
    48	
    49	Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.
    50	
    51	Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
    52	
    53	Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
    54	
    55	Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.
    56
