to use the fully built AI document-parsing / onboarding page — drag any files
onto the dropzone to watch the simulated Claude extraction, review low-confidence
rows, and confirm. **Chat assistant** is also fully interactive.

| Trips & coaches | 3 | Desmond | scaffold |
| Exception inbox | 5 | Jayden | scaffold |
| QR check-in | mobile | Vimal | scaffold |

The frontend ships with simulated data so it runs standalone. To connect the
Express + PostgreSQL backend described in `HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md`:

1. Set `VITE_API_URL` to your API origin.
2. In `src/lib/claudeParse.js`, set `USE_SIMULATION = false`.
3. Run migration `001_init.sql` (the DDL from the HLD) and seed dev data.

trip assistant), so the shared team API seat / key never reaches the browser.

content.text:
I've now read every file. Their frontend builds cleanly. Here's the full picture.

## What their repo has that we're missing

**A real, working shared backend.** `backend/server.js` + `data.js` on Express + `pg` (Postgres) — already Neon-compatible, auto-detecting SSL from `DATABASE_URL`. It auto-creates its schema and seeds a trip, 4 coaches, and a login on first run. Nobody sets up tables by hand.

**A permission system, not just roles.** `permissions.js` at the repo root is imported by *both* frontend and backend: `manageDelegates`, `exportData`, `manageAccounts`. Routes are gated with `requirePermission("...")`, and there's an `AccountControlPage` for managing accounts. This is more sophisticated than the plain `staff`/`admin` role I stubbed.

**Real auth with live session revocation.** `POST /api/auth/login` takes `{ staffId, password }` (not email), returns a base64 demo token plus a permissions object. `GET /api/auth/session` re-reads permissions from the DB so someone can be logged out mid-session. Login is `staff_194` / `password123!`.

**Two governing documents I hadn't seen.** `HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md` contains the authoritative DDL and REST API table — **including your endpoints**. `PROJECT_IMPLEMENTATION_PHASE.md` assigns you: exception CRUD + inbox, the Log Exception mobile flow, manual override, and the QR-fallback path shared with Vimal.

**An explicit ownership convention.** Every base file carries a "DO NOT edit this file" banner from Jun Qi, and `server.js` has a marked **TEAMMATE ZONE** where you mount your own router:
```js
import exceptionsRouter from "./routes/exceptions.js";
app.use(exceptionsRouter);
```

**Also: `AccountControlPage`, an Excel export endpoint, a `/api` dev proxy, and `apiDelete`** — which their `api.js` has and my old copy didn't.

## Where my build conflicts with theirs

This is the important part, and it's not a small list.

| Thing | Mine | Theirs (authoritative) |
|---|---|---|
| Exception table | `exceptions` | **`exception_tickets`** |
| Issue column | `issue_type` | **`type`** |
| Idempotency key | `client_ref` | **`client_event_id`** |
| Endpoints | `/api/exceptions` | **`/api/trips/:id/exceptions`** |
| Login body | `{ email }` | **`{ staffId, password }`** |
| Auth model | my own JWT + `staff`/`admin` | **their token + permissions object** |
| Attendance table | `attendance` | **`check_in_logs`** |
| Delegate IDs | `d-lim`, `trip-bj` | **`d-1`…, trip `t-1`, coaches `c1`–`c4`** |
| Statuses | OPEN/RESOLVED/CANCELLED | **OPEN/RESOLVED only** |

Two more things worth flagging:

**Their live backend doesn't create your tables.** `data.js` only creates `trips`, `coaches`, `delegates`, `accounts` — no `exception_tickets`, no `check_in_logs`. The HLD specifies them, but nobody's implemented them. That's *your* job, and since you can't edit `data.js`, your router needs to create its own tables on startup.

**A real bug you should raise with the team:** `frontend/src/lib/api.js` imports `../../../permissions.js` — a file *outside* the `frontend/` folder. Vite's dev server handles it via `fs.allow: ['..']`, and `vite build` worked here. But when Vercel deploys with `frontend/` as the root directory, that parent file won't exist in the build context and the deploy will fail. Worth flagging now, not on deployment day.

## How to integrate — the approach that respects their rules

**Backend:** create `backend/routes/exceptions.js` (a new file — you own it), exporting a Router that (a) creates `exception_tickets` + `check_in_logs` with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and (b) implements the HLD's endpoints. Mount it with two lines in the TEAMMATE ZONE. Nothing of Jun Qi's is touched.

**Admin frontend:** drop in `pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx` (replacing their scaffold — it's tagged *Owner · Jayden*), plus your CSS and modal, and rewrite your data layer to use *their* `api.js` (`apiGet`/`apiPost`/`apiPatch`/`apiDelete`) so you inherit their token handling for free. Their `App.jsx` and `Sidebar.jsx` already route `/exceptions` to you — no edits needed to either.

**On-ground app:** stays a separate app. It just points at the same backend and calls the same endpoints.

The real work is a **contract adaptation**: renaming tables/columns/endpoints to match the HLD, and swapping my auth stub for their token. Your UI, CSS, business rules, QR scanner, and alert logic all survive unchanged.

One thing genuinely undecided that you should ask the team about: **the HLD says nothing about real-time push.** My critical-alert feature uses SSE, and their backend has no WebSocket/SSE layer. Your "push to all staff devices" requirement needs *some* transport — SSE is the simplest thing that fits their Express app, but it means adding something the HLD didn't plan for, and Vimal/Vance may have assumptions here.

Want me to do the adaptation now — build `backend/routes/exceptions.js` against their exact HLD schema, rewire both frontends to their `api.js` and auth, and verify it end-to-end against a real Postgres? I'd deliver it as a drop-in patch: only files you own, nothing of theirs edited.

input.file_text:
# Exception Logging — Integration Notes (Jayden)

My feature is now integrated into the VJMDynamics base repo. This file records exactly what was added, the one shared line I had to touch, and the decisions that need a team ruling.

## Files I added (all mine)

```
backend/routes/exceptions.js          Feature router: tickets, alerts, manual override, SSE
backend/seed-demo.js                  Demo roster + sample tickets  (npm run seed:demo)
frontend/src/lib/exceptionsApi.js     Data layer, built on the shared lib/api.js
frontend/src/components/LogExceptionModal.jsx
frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx    (replaces the scaffold tagged "Owner · Jayden")
frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.css
```

## Files I changed (minimal, declared)

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/server.js` | 2 lines in the **TEAMMATE ZONE** — import + `app.use(exceptionsRouter)` | The zone exists for exactly this |
| `backend/server.js` | 1 line: `.then(initExceptions)` in the startup chain | My tables must be created *after* the base schema, since they hold foreign keys into `trips`, `delegates` and `accounts`. This is outside the TEAMMATE ZONE — **flagged for JQ's approval.** |
| `backend/package.json` | added `"seed:demo"` script | additive only |

I did **not** touch `data.js`, `permissions.js`, `lib/api.js`, `Layout.jsx`, `Sidebar.jsx`, `App.jsx`, or any teammate page. `App.jsx` already routes `/exceptions` to my page and `Sidebar.jsx` already links it, so no edits were needed.

## Reusing the base rather than duplicating it

- **Auth:** my router resolves the caller by importing JQ's exported `getAccountByUsername` and decoding the same `demo.<base64(username)>.token` her `/api/auth/login` issues. No second login flow, no duplicated password logic.
- **HTTP:** the frontend data layer calls the shared `apiGet/apiPost/apiPatch/apiDelete`, so it inherits token storage, "keep me signed in", and typed errors (`err.status`, `err.code`).
- **UI:** priority and status pills use the existing `StatusBadge`; all colour/spacing come from `tokens.css`. My CSS is scoped to `.exc-*` and adds no global rules.

## Database

Two tables from `HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md` §2, created idempotently on boot (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) so Vimal's check-in module can be added later without a migration clash:

- `exception_tickets` (§7) — mine
- `check_in_logs` (§6) — shared with Vimal; this module writes only the `MANUAL` rows

### Deviations from the HLD (deliberate)

1. **`VARCHAR(64)` ids, not `UUID`.** The HLD types ids as UUID, but the live schema in `data.js` uses `VARCHAR(64)` (`t-1`, `c1`, `d-1`). A foreign key must match its parent's type, so my tables follow the live schema. Ids are still UUID *values*, generated with `randomUUID()`.
2. **`raised_by` / `resolved_by` reference `accounts(id)`, not `users(id)`.** The HLD's `users` table doesn't exist yet; `accounts` is what the base actually implements.
3. **Real-time push is not in the HLD.** The "alert all staff devices" requirement needs a transport, so I added Server-Sent Events at `GET /api/exceptions/stream`. It needs no new dependency and passes through restrictive proxies. **This is the item most worth a team decision** — if Vimal or Vance are assuming WebSockets, we should align.

## Endpoints (per HLD §3.6)

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/trips/:id/exceptions?status=&priority=` | List tickets + counts |
| GET | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Single ticket |
| POST | `/api/trips/:id/exceptions` | Raise a ticket (CRITICAL → push) |
| PATCH | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Resolve, or change priority/note |
| DELETE | `/api/exceptions/:id` | Remove a ticket raised in error |
| POST | `/api/checkins/manual` | Manual attendance override |
| GET | `/api/exceptions/stream` | Live alert channel (SSE) |

`POST /api/checkins` (the QR path) is intentionally **not** implemented here — that's Vimal's. I namespaced mine to `/checkins/manual` so both routers can mount side by side.

## Two things worth raising with the team

1. **`CANCELLED` no longer exists.** The HLD's `exception_status` enum is `OPEN | RESOLVED` only, so a ticket raised in error is now hard-deleted rather than soft-cancelled. That loses the audit trail. If we want it back, we add `CANCELLED` to the enum — a one-line HLD change, but it needs agreeing, not assuming.
2. **A real deployment bug in the base.** `frontend/src/lib/api.js` imports `../../../permissions.js`, a file *outside* `frontend/`. Vite's dev server allows it via `fs.allow: ['..']` and `vite build` works locally — but when Vercel builds with `frontend/` as the root directory, that parent file won't be in the build context and the deploy will fail. Worth fixing before deployment day, not on it.

## Running it

```bash
# 1. Database — put your Neon connection string in backend/.env
cd backend
cp .env.example .env          # set DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]
npm install
npm start                     # creates every table on first boot

# 2. Demo data (delegates + sample tickets) — once, in a second terminal
npm run seed:demo

# 3. Frontend
cd ../frontend
npm install
npm run dev                   # http://localhost:5173  (proxies /api to :4000)
```

Sign in with **`staff_194` / `password123!`**, then open **Exceptions** in the sidebar.

A local Postgres works too — leave `DATABASE_URL` pointing at `localhost` and SSL switches off automatically.

## Verified

Against a real PostgreSQL database, end to end:

- Boot creates `exception_tickets` + `check_in_logs` alongside the base tables.
- Login through the team's own login page issues a token my routes accept; an unauthenticated request gets `401`, a bad SSE token gets `401`.
- Inbox renders real joined data (delegate, coach, raiser, VIP flag) with counts `{all, critical, open, resolved}`.
- Create → the ticket appears in Postgres; a repeated `clientEventId` returns the original (idempotent, `duplicate: true`).
- Resolve → `RESOLVED`; resolving again returns `409`. Delete → `404` on the second attempt.
- Manual override writes a `MANUAL` row to `check_in_logs` and flips the delegate to `PRESENT`, which the dashboard head-count picks up.
- All of JQ's base routes still pass: dashboard, session, delegates, accounts, missing view, and the Excel export (`HTTP 200`).
- Responsive: table on desktop, cards on mobile.

content.text:
Done. `mustergo-integrated.zip` is the team's repo with your feature fully integrated, running against real PostgreSQL end to end.

**How it runs**
```bash
cd backend && cp .env.example .env   # paste your Neon DATABASE_URL
npm install && npm start             # creates your tables on first boot
npm run seed:demo                    # delegates + sample tickets
cd ../frontend && npm install && npm run dev
```
Sign in with `staff_194 / password123!`, click **Exceptions**.

**What I built, and what I deliberately didn't touch**

Your feature is a self-contained module: `backend/routes/exceptions.js` mounted with the two lines their TEAMMATE ZONE explicitly invites, plus the page, modal, CSS, and a data layer built on *their* `api.js`. I did **not** edit `data.js`, `permissions.js`, `api.js`, `Layout.jsx`, `Sidebar.jsx`, or `App.jsx` — their router already points `/exceptions` at your page, so nothing needed changing.

Rather than duplicate their auth, your router decodes the same token their `/api/auth/login` issues by importing Jun Qi's exported `getAccountByUsername`. One login, one session, no parallel auth system.

**One edit outside the TEAMMATE ZONE**, which I've flagged prominently in the notes: a single `.then(initExceptions)` in the startup chain. Your tables hold foreign keys into `trips`, `delegates`, and `accounts`, so they must be created *after* the base schema. Worth mentioning to Jun Qi rather than letting her find it.

**Verified against real Postgres** — 17 automated browser checks, all passing. Counts came back `{all:8, critical:2, open:3, resolved:5}`, a ticket created through the UI landed in the database, a repeated `clientEventId` returned the original (idempotent), double-resolve gave `409`, manual override wrote a `MANUAL` row to `check_in_logs` and flipped the delegate to `PRESENT`. Every one of Jun Qi's routes still passes, including the Excel export.

I also found and fixed a real bug of my own along the way: the "Live" indicator only lit up when an event arrived, so it would sit at "Connecting…" forever on a quiet trip. It now reacts to the SSE connection opening.

**Three things that need a team decision, not my assumption:**

1. **`CANCELLED` is gone.** The HLD's enum is `OPEN | RESOLVED` only, so tickets raised in error are now hard-deleted instead of soft-cancelled — you lose the audit trail. Restoring it is a one-line enum change, but it's a spec change.
2. **Real-time push isn't in the HLD at all.** Your "alert all staff devices" requirement needs *some* transport; I used SSE. If Vimal or Vance assumed WebSockets, align now.
3. **A deployment bug in their base, not yours.** `frontend/src/lib/api.js` imports `../../../permissions.js` — a file outside `frontend/`. It builds locally, but Vercel with `frontend/` as root won't have that parent file and the deploy will fail. Better raised now than on deployment day.

Want me to bring the on-ground app into this repo next, or prep the AI-workflow log for C1/C2 while this session is fresh?

text:
Into a file called **`backend/.env`** — which doesn't exist yet. You create it by copying the example:

```bash
cd backend
cp .env.example .env
```

Then open `backend/.env` and replace the placeholder on the `DATABASE_URL` line:

```bash
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]
```

with the string Neon gives you, which looks like:

```bash
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]
```

Three things worth knowing:

**Keep `?sslmode=require` on the end.** Neon requires TLS. The code auto-detects this — it enables SSL for any non-localhost host — so as long as you paste the full string Neon shows you, it just works.

**Get the string from:** Neon dashboard → your project → **Connection Details** → copy the connection string (choose the "Node.js" or plain `psql` variant; both are the same URL). If it's your teammate's project, ask him for it rather than creating a second database — your `exception_tickets` table has foreign keys into the `delegates`, `trips`, and `accounts` tables, so it has to live in the *same* database as everyone else's data.

**Don't commit it.** `backend/.gitignore` already excludes `.env`, which is why only `.env.example` is in the repo. That file has a real password in it — keep it out of Git and out of Slack.

Then, from `backend/`:

```bash
npm install
npm start          # first boot creates every table, including yours
npm run seed:demo  # second terminal, once — adds delegates + sample tickets
```

If the connection string is wrong you'll see the startup fail immediately with a connection error rather than a confusing error later — the base code deliberately fails fast on boot. A successful start prints `PostgreSQL connected` followed by `Exception module ready -> exception_tickets, check_in_logs`.

text:
That's Windows — `cp` is a Unix command. On Windows Command Prompt the equivalent is `copy`:

```cmd
cd backend
copy .env.example .env
```

If you're in **PowerShell** instead, either of these works:

```powershell
cd backend
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

(PowerShell also aliases `cp` to `Copy-Item`, so `cp .env.example .env` works there — the error tells me you're in Command Prompt, not PowerShell.)

Honestly, the simplest path is to skip the command line entirely: in VS Code, right-click `.env.example` in the file explorer → **Copy**, right-click the `backend` folder → **Paste**, then rename the copy to `.env`. Nothing magic happens during the copy; you just need a file named `.env` sitting next to `.env.example`.

One Windows gotcha to watch for: File Explorer hides extensions by default, so if you create the file through Explorer you can end up with `.env.txt` without seeing it. VS Code doesn't do this, which is another reason to make the file there.

Once it exists, open `backend/.env` and replace the `DATABASE_URL=` line with your Neon connection string, then:

```cmd
npm install
npm start
```

Could not connect to MySQL. Is your MySQL server running?

text:
Ignore the words "MySQL" — that message is stale text in your teammate's `server.js` from before the team moved to Postgres. It prints on *any* database connection failure. The real signal is **`ECONNREFUSED`**: nothing accepted the connection, meaning your app never reached Neon.

That almost always means `DATABASE_URL` isn't being read, so `pg` fell back to its default of `localhost:5432` — where nothing is running. Work through these in order:

**1. Is the file named exactly `.env`?**
Not `.env.txt`, not `env`, not `.env.example`. Check from `backend/`:
```cmd
dir /a
```
You should see `.env` listed. If you see `.env.txt`, rename it.

**2. Is it in `backend/`?**
It must sit next to `server.js` and `data.js` — not at the repo root. The code calls `dotenv/config` from inside `backend/`.

**3. Is the line uncommented and unquoted?**
Open `backend/.env`. It should look like this, with no leading `#`, no spaces around `=`, and **no quotes**:
```
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]
```
A common mistake is leaving the placeholder line *and* adding yours below it — the first one wins. Delete the placeholder.

**4. Confirm Node actually sees it.** From `backend/`, run:
```cmd
node -e "require('dotenv').config(); console.log(process.env.DATABASE_URL ? 'FOUND: ' + process.env.DATABASE_URL.slice(0,30) + '...' : 'NOT FOUND')"
```
If that prints `NOT FOUND`, the problem is the file (steps 1–3). If it prints `FOUND: postgresql://...`, the file is fine and the issue is the connection string itself.

**If it says FOUND but you still get ECONNREFUSED**, the likely causes are:
- The string is a **psql command** rather than a URL. Neon's dashboard sometimes shows `psql 'postgresql://...'` — copy only the part starting at `postgresql://`, without the `psql` or the quotes.
- You copied a **pooled vs direct** string incorrectly, or the string is truncated mid-paste. It must end with your database name plus `?sslmode=require`.
- Your network blocks outbound port 5432. School Wi-Fi sometimes does. Try a phone hotspot to test — if it connects, that's the culprit.

Tell me what step 4 prints and I can narrow it down from there.

text: how can i run the application without starting the databse

content.text: how can i run the application without starting the databse

text:
Short answer: **the integrated app can't run without a database** — and that's by design, not a bug. Their `server.js` calls `initDb()` and refuses to start if it fails, the login page authenticates against the `accounts` table, and my inbox reads real tickets. There's no meaningful "integrated app" without Postgres behind it.

So you've got three real options, depending on what you're actually trying to do.

**If you just need to demo the UI right now** — use the standalone build I made you earlier (`mustergo-exception-standalone.zip`). It ships with `USE_SIMULATION = true`, no login, no backend, no database:
```cmd
npm install
npm run dev
```
That's exactly what it was built for, and it's still the safest thing to put in front of a reviewer.

**If you want the integrated app but Neon isn't cooperating** — run Postgres locally instead. Download the installer from postgresql.org, then in `backend/.env`:
```
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]
```
Create the `mustergo` database once (pgAdmin ships with the installer, or `createdb mustergo`). SSL switches off automatically for `localhost`, so nothing else changes. Everything else — `npm start`, `npm run seed:demo` — works identically. This is genuinely worth doing anyway: it means you can develop on a plane, and you're not sharing a database with four teammates while you experiment.

**If you want to fix Neon** — we were mid-diagnosis. Run this from `backend/` and tell me what it prints:
```cmd
node -e "require('dotenv').config(); console.log(process.env.DATABASE_URL ? 'FOUND: ' + process.env.DATABASE_URL.slice(0,40) : 'NOT FOUND')"
```
`ECONNREFUSED` means nothing accepted the connection, which nearly always means the env var wasn't read and `pg` fell back to `localhost`.

---

There is a fourth option: I could add a `USE_SIMULATION` flag to the *integrated* frontend so it fakes the API and bypasses login. I'd rather not push you toward it, though — it means maintaining a fake copy of your teammate's auth and delegate data, and it's the kind of thing that drifts out of sync and hides real integration bugs. The standalone build already fills that need cleanly.

Which direction do you want — local Postgres, or keep debugging Neon?

text:
That's not an error — that's your backend **working correctly**. Your database connected, the server booted, and it's answering requests.

Port 4000 is the API. It only serves `/api/*` routes; there's nothing at `/`, so it correctly returns a 404 for that path. That JSON is coming from the fallback handler at the bottom of `server.js`.

Confirm it's healthy by visiting:
```
http://localhost:4000/api/health
```
You should get `{"ok":true,"service":"mustergo-backend"}`.

**The website is on a different port.** The backend serves data; the React app is served by Vite. Open a **second terminal**, leave the backend running in the first, and:

```cmd
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then go to **http://localhost:5173** — that's your actual app. Vite proxies every `/api` request through to port 4000 behind the scenes, which is why both need to be running at once.

Sign in with `staff_194` / `password123!`, then click **Exceptions** in the sidebar.

One thing before you do: if you haven't run it yet, seed the demo data, or your inbox and delegate picker will be empty. In the backend terminal, stop the server (`Ctrl+C`), then:

```cmd
npm run seed:demo
npm start
```

That adds the nine delegates and seven sample tickets. You should see `Seeded 9 delegates.` and `Seeded 7 exception tickets.`

Good news first: **Neon is connected.** `PostgreSQL connected -> neondb_owner@ep-purple-heart...` and `Exception module ready` both printed — your database, your tables, all working. The SSL warning above it is harmless, just pg telling you about a future version change; ignore it.

The actual error is different: `EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::4000`. Something is **already sitting on port 4000** — almost certainly a previous `node server.js` you ran earlier (maybe during the seeding steps) that never fully stopped, especially if a terminal window got closed instead of properly `Ctrl+C`'d.

**Find and stop it, on Windows:**

```cmd
netstat -ano | findstr :4000
```

This prints a line ending in a PID (a number), e.g.:
```
TCP    0.0.0.0:4000    0.0.0.0:0    LISTENING    16204
```

Kill that process:
```cmd
taskkill /PID 16204 /F
```
(swap in whatever number you actually see)

Then run `npm start` again — it should bind cleanly this time.

**If that doesn't find anything**, check for a stray `node.exe` in Task Manager (Details tab) and end it there instead.

**Going forward**, always stop the server with `Ctrl+C` in its own terminal rather than closing the window — that's almost certainly how you ended up with an orphaned process holding the port.

text:
The user is probably seeing this error on the frontend login page. The backend is running on port 4000 now, but the frontend can't connect to it—could be a misconfigured API URL in the environment variables, CORS issues, the Vite proxy not working properly, or the backend crashed after we fixed the port conflict. Let me walk through the troubleshooting steps to figure out what's actually happening.That message means the frontend tried to call the API and got nothing back. A few likely causes, in order of probability:

**1. Is the backend actually still running?** After killing that stuck process, did `npm start` in the backend terminal stay up, or did it exit? Check that terminal window right now — you should still see `Exception module ready` and no crash below it. If that terminal is closed or shows an error, the backend isn't running and needs restarting.

**2. Confirm it's actually listening.** Open a fresh terminal (don't touch the backend one) and run:
```cmd
curl http://localhost:4000/api/health
```
You should get `{"ok":true,"service":"mustergo-backend"}`. If this fails too, the backend is the problem — go back to terminal 1.
If this **works**, the backend is fine and the problem is specifically the frontend not reaching it — go to step 3.

**3. Check for a stray `frontend/.env` overriding the API URL.** The frontend's Vite dev server automatically proxies `/api` to port 4000 — but only if nothing overrides `VITE_API_URL`. Check:
```cmd
cd frontend
dir /a
```
If you see a `.env` file in there (not `.env_Future.example` — an actual `.env`), open it. If it sets `VITE_API_URL` to something other than empty/unset, that's likely your problem — delete that line or delete the file. You shouldn't need a `frontend/.env` at all for local dev; only `backend/.env` is required.

**4. Restart the frontend after any `.env` change.** Vite only reads env files at startup — if you just created/edited one, stop the frontend (`Ctrl+C`) and run `npm run dev` again.

**5. Hard-refresh the browser tab.** Sometimes a cached failed request lingers. `Ctrl+Shift+R` on the login page.

Run step 2 first and tell me what it returns — that tells us immediately whether this is a backend problem or a frontend-to-backend wiring problem.

text:
The backend is responding fine, so the issue must be on the frontend side—either the dev server isn't running with the proper proxy configuration, or the fetch request is failing to reach the API endpoint. I should track down where that "Can't reach the server" error message originates in their code, likely from a catch block in the login or API layer that fires when the network request fails entirely.

Looking at the most probable causes: the user might be accessing the frontend through the wrong method—opening the HTML file directly, using vite preview instead of the dev server, or running it on a different port where the proxy isn't configured. The CORS settings shouldn't be blocking since the proxy should handle same-origin requests, and the vite config has the backend target hardcoded to localhost:4000. Windows firewall is unlikely, but I should consider whether the frontend is actually being served by the dev server at all or if it's being loaded statically without the proxy layer. The error message in LoginPage.jsx's catch block triggers when fetch fails with a network error, which would happen if VITE_API_URL points to an unreachable absolute URL or if the Vite dev server proxy isn't active. This makes me wonder if they're running `npm run preview` instead of `npm run dev` — the proxy configuration only works in the dev server, not the preview server, which would explain why the login fails even though the page loads.

Another possibility is they're opening the page through a different method entirely, like VSCode's Live Server extension, which would bypass Vite completely. I should ask them to confirm they're running `npm run dev` and check that the URL bar shows `localhost:5173`, not a file path or a different port. I also need to verify whether CORS is even a factor here — if they're using the Vite dev proxy correctly, requests are same-origin and CORS shouldn't apply, but if the frontend is somehow making direct requests to `http://localhost:4000/api` without going through the proxy, then CORS headers from the backend would matter.Good — the backend is confirmed healthy, so this is specifically about the frontend not reaching it. Before I diagnose further, I need to rule out one common cause: how you're actually running the frontend matters here, because only the **dev server** proxies `/api` calls to port 4000 — a production preview doesn't.

Two things to check:

**1. What's in your browser's address bar right now?** It needs to be exactly `http://localhost:5173`. Not `127.0.0.1:5500`, not a `file://` path, not `5174`. If you have a VS Code extension like Live Server running, or you double-clicked `index.html`, that would open the page without Vite's dev server behind it — meaning no proxy exists, and every `/api` call fails exactly like this.

**2. What command is running in your frontend terminal?** It must say `vite` (from `npm run dev`), not `vite preview`. Run:
```cmd
cd frontend
npm run dev
```
and confirm it prints something like:
```
VITE v5.x.x  ready in ...
➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
```
Then open that exact URL.

**3. While you're at it, hard-check the connection directly from the browser console.** On the login page, press F12 to open DevTools → Console tab, and run:
```js
fetch('/api/health').then(r => r.json()).then(console.log).catch(console.error)
```
If that prints `{ok: true, ...}`, the proxy works and something else is wrong. If it throws an error, tell me exactly what the console shows — that error message will say precisely what failed (connection refused, CORS, wrong URL, etc.) instead of the generic message the login page shows you.

Run that fetch and paste what comes back — that'll tell us exactly where this is breaking.

The port difference doesn't matter since Vite finds the next available one, but the 401 error points to an authentication issue—either the credentials were entered incorrectly or the database doesn't have the seeded staff_194 account, possibly because they're connected to a fresh database where the accounts table exists but the seed data was never populated.

I should walk them through checking for typos and trailing spaces in their credentials, verifying the accounts table actually contains the staff_194 row by querying the database directly, and confirming they're consistently using the same database project.Progress — the request is reaching the backend now (401 is a real response, not a connection failure). A 401 here specifically means `POST /api/auth/login` ran and the backend rejected the credentials as wrong.

A few things to check, in order:

**1. Exact credentials, no typos/spaces.**
- Staff ID: `staff_194` (underscore, not a space or dash)
- Password: `password123!` (the exclamation mark is part of it)

If your browser autofilled saved credentials from a different site, clear both fields and type these fresh.

**2. Confirm the account actually exists in *this* Neon database.** The seeded login is created automatically the first time `initDb()` runs against an empty `accounts` table — but if you've connected to more than one Neon project/database while troubleshooting (e.g., switched connection strings), it's possible the database your backend is *currently* pointed at doesn't have that row yet.

Check directly — open a new terminal:
```cmd
cd backend
node -e "require('dotenv').config(); import('./data.js').then(async d => { await d.initDb(); const a = await d.getAccountByUsername('staff_194'); console.log(a); })"
```
This should print the account object (username, role, etc.). If it prints `undefined` or `null`, the account genuinely doesn't exist in that database, and `initDb()` should create it — try restarting the backend fully (`Ctrl+C` then `npm start`) and watch for `Login: staff_194 / password123!` in the startup log.

**3. Notice the port — 5175, not 5173.** That means something was already holding 5173 and 5174 when Vite started (probably leftover processes from earlier troubleshooting). Not the cause of this 401, but worth cleaning up:
```cmd
netstat -ano | findstr :517
```
and `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` on any old ones, so you're not accumulating orphaned dev servers.

Run step 2 first — that tells us definitively whether the account exists in the database you're currently connected to.

Fixed. Four files changed — grab `mustergo-integrated-updated.zip`, or drop in the four individual files if you'd rather patch by hand.

**How the badge works now**

- **Backend** — new `GET /api/trips/:id/exceptions/critical-count`, returning just an integer. A dedicated endpoint rather than reusing the ticket list, because the sidebar renders on *every* page and shouldn't pull the whole inbox each time. I also added `criticalOpen` to the counts on the main list endpoint.
- **`useCriticalCount.js`** (new, yours) — fetches on mount, refreshes on every SSE ticket event, plus a slow 60s poll as a safety net if the stream drops. Swallows errors so a failed count can never break the app shell.
- **`Layout.jsx`** — the hardcoded `const openExceptions = 3` is now `useCriticalCount()`.

`Sidebar.jsx` needed no change: it already renders `{badge ? ... : null}`, so a count of 0 hides the badge automatically.

**Verified against the live stack** — four checks, all passing:
- Seeded state (1 unresolved critical) → badge shows **1**, not 3
- Log a second critical → badge updates to **2** live, without a refresh
- Resolve both → badge **disappears** entirely (no "0")
- Log a *normal*-priority ticket → badge **stays hidden**, exactly as you specified

**Two things worth flagging:**

`Layout.jsx` is one of Jun Qi's "do not edit" files. I kept the change to two lines — an import and one assignment — by putting all the fetching logic in my own hook file. But it *is* an edit to her file, so tell her rather than let her discover it. That's now the second such edit, alongside the `.then(initExceptions)` line in `server.js`.

On the bcrypt change: my exceptions router authenticates by decoding their `demo.<base64>.token` format. Both pieces confirmed. Here's the answer.

## This is not your bug, and not your file

**It's an internal bug in Jun Qi's auth code.** Specifically: *half of a password-hashing upgrade landed.*

Something now **writes** a bcrypt hash (`$2b$10$...`) into `accounts.password` — but the login check in `server.js` still does a **plain string comparison**:

```js
if (!acc || acc.password !== password) { ...401... }
```

That's why typing the hash works: you're literally handing it the exact string that's stored. And `password123!` fails, because nobody ever calls `bcrypt.compare()`. The two halves don't meet.

Proof it's a plaintext comparison: if login actually used bcrypt, typing the hash would **fail** and `password123!` would **succeed**. You're seeing the exact inverse.

## Why the error message is misleading

That's a **second, separate bug**, also in her `LoginPage.jsx`. It picks the error message by string-matching:

```js
if (msg.includes("401"))      → "Incorrect Staff ID or password."
else if (msg.includes("400")) → "Please enter your Staff ID and password."
else                          → "Can't reach the server..."
```

Somewhere in the bcrypt change, the thrown error stopped carrying `401` in its `.message`, so it falls through to the `else`. The server is fine — it's returning a correct 401 — the UI is just mislabelling it. That sent us both chasing a connection problem that never existed. Worth telling her; it'll waste other teammates' time too.

## Should *you* fix it?

**No — report it.** `server.js` (auth) and `data.js` (accounts) are hers, and you've already got two edits to her files to explain. Adding a third, in the auth path, is exactly where a merge conflict hurts. It's also genuinely her design decision whether to hash.

Send her something like:

> The `accounts.password` column now stores a bcrypt hash, but `POST /api/auth/login` in `server.js:115` still compares `acc.password !== password` as plaintext — so `password123!` is rejected and pasting the raw hash logs you in. Needs `bcrypt.compare(password, acc.password)`. Two other spots need it too: `createAccount` / `updateAccount` in `data.js` must hash on write, and `LoginPage.jsx:81` shows "Can't reach the server" for a 401 because the error's `.message` no longer contains "401".

## To unblock yourself right now

Don't paste the hash around. Reset that one row back to what the login code actually expects. Against your Neon database:

```sql
UPDATE accounts SET password = 'password123!' WHERE username = 'staff_194';
```

Run it in the **Neon SQL Editor** (dashboard → your project → SQL Editor). Then `password123!` logs you in again, and you can carry on with your own work while she fixes the auth properly.

That's a deliberate step *backwards* on security, so treat it as temporary and local to the demo database. Once she lands `bcrypt.compare()`, delete that row (or let `initDb()` reseed it) so the hashed password takes over. Don't do this on anything real — but for a shared school demo DB whose seeded credentials are already printed in the console at every boot, it changes nothing that wasn't already public.

text:
Git isn't installed on your machine (or isn't on your PATH). That's expected if you've never used it — GitHub's website doesn't require it, but the command line does.

## Install Git

Download from **https://git-scm.com/download/win** and run the installer. Accept all the defaults — the important one is already default: *"Git from the command line and also from 3rd-party software"*, which is what puts `git` on your PATH.

Then **close and reopen your terminal** (PATH changes don't apply to already-open windows — this trips people up constantly). Verify:

```cmd
git --version
```

If that prints a version number, you're set. If it still fails after reopening, restart VS Code entirely, or reboot.

## First-time setup

Git needs to know who you are before it'll let you commit:

```cmd
git config --global user.name "Jayden"
git config --global user.email "your-github-email@example.com"
```

Use the same email as your GitHub account, or your commits won't be linked to your profile.

---

## A simpler alternative worth considering

Since you're new to this and the stakes are "don't clobber my team's repo," you might prefer **GitHub Desktop** (https://desktop.github.com). It's a GUI: you clone your repo, it shows you a checklist of exactly which files changed, you tick them, write a message, and click *Commit* then *Push*. Same result, and crucially it makes Step 5 — *"look at what you're about to commit"* — visual and hard to skip.

The advice I gave you doesn't change at all. You still:
1. Update your branch from `main` first
2. Copy in your **new** files
3. **Hand-edit** `server.js`, `Layout.jsx`, `package.json` — never overwrite them
4. Review the changed-files list before committing
5. Push, then open a Pull Request

GitHub Desktop just replaces the typing in steps 1, 4, and 5.

**One thing that doesn't change either way:** VS Code also has Git built into its Source Control panel (the branch icon in the left sidebar) — but it still needs Git itself installed. So install Git regardless; then pick whichever interface you prefer.

Install it, reopen your terminal, run `git --version`, and tell me what you get.

input.file_text:
# Pushing your Exception feature to the team repo A complete walkthrough. Follow it top to bottom. Don't skip Step 0 or Step 6. **The golden rule:** you are adding 8 files and hand-editing 3 lines in 3 shared files. You are **not** replacing the folder. If you ever find yourself deleting your teammates' files, stop — something has gone wrong. --- ## Step 0 — Understand what you're about to do (2 min read) Your `mustergo-integrated-updated` folder is a **snapshot** of the team repo taken a while ago, plus your work. Since you took that snapshot, teammates changed things (someone added bcrypt password hashing). If you copy your whole folder over the branch, you **delete their bcrypt work**. Git won't warn you. It'll look like you did it on purpose. So instead: copy in only the files that are yours, and hand-edit the 3 shared files. Here is the exact inventory: | Category | Files | What to do | |---|---|---| | **New — yours alone** | `backend/routes/exceptions.js`
`backend/seed-demo.js`
`frontend/src/lib/exceptionsApi.js`
`frontend/src/lib/useCriticalCount.js`
`frontend/src/components/LogExceptionModal.jsx`
`frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.css`
`INTEGRATION_NOTES_JAYDEN.md` | Copy in. They don't exist yet, nothing to break. | | **Replaces your own scaffold** | `frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx` | Copy in (overwrite). It's tagged `Owner · Jayden`. | | **Shared — DO NOT overwrite** | `backend/server.js`
`frontend/src/components/Layout.jsx`
`backend/package.json` | Open and hand-edit. 3 small edits total. | | **Never touch** | `data.js`, `permissions.js`, `lib/api.js`, `LoginPage.jsx`, everything else | Leave alone. | The first 8 files are prepared for you in the **`FILES_TO_COPY`** folder, already in the correct folder structure. --- ## Step 1 — Install Git 1. Go to **https://git-scm.com/download/win** and run the installer. 2. Click **Next** through every screen (defaults are correct). 3. **Close VS Code completely and reopen it.** Git won't be found until you do. 4. In VS Code, open a terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**) and type: ``` git --version ``` You should see something like `git version 2.4x.x`. If you see "not recognized", restart your computer and try again. 5. Tell Git who you are (once, ever): ``` git config --global user.name "Jayden" git config --global user.email "your-github-email@example.com" ``` Use the same email as your GitHub account. --- ## Step 2 — Update your branch before you add anything Your branch is out of date with `main`. Pull in your teammates' latest work **first**, so you're building on top of it rather than beside it. In the VS Code terminal, inside your repo folder: ``` git checkout main git pull git checkout your-branch-name git merge main ``` Replace `your-branch-name` with your actual branch (e.g. `jayden`). **What you should see:** either `Already up to date.` or a summary of files that changed. **If you see the word `CONFLICT`:** stop. Don't fix it yourself yet. Note which files conflicted and ask me. --- ## Step 3 — Copy in your 8 files Open **two File Explorer windows** side by side: - Window A: the `FILES_TO_COPY` folder - Window B: your repo folder (the one VS Code has open) Now copy each file into the matching location. The folder structure in `FILES_TO_COPY` mirrors the repo exactly, so paths line up: ``` FILES_TO_COPY/backend/routes/exceptions.js → /backend/routes/exceptions.js FILES_TO_COPY/backend/seed-demo.js → /backend/seed-demo.js FILES_TO_COPY/frontend/src/lib/exceptionsApi.js → /frontend/src/lib/exceptionsApi.js FILES_TO_COPY/frontend/src/lib/useCriticalCount.js → /frontend/src/lib/useCriticalCount.js FILES_TO_COPY/frontend/src/components/LogExceptionModal.jsx → /frontend/src/components/LogExceptionModal.jsx FILES_TO_COPY/frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx → /frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx FILES_TO_COPY/frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.css → /frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.css FILES_TO_COPY/INTEGRATION_NOTES_JAYDEN.md → /INTEGRATION_NOTES_JAYDEN.md ``` Notes: - **`backend/routes/` probably doesn't exist yet.** Create the folder first (right-click in `backend` → New Folder → name it `routes`). - Windows will ask to confirm replacing `ExceptionInboxPage.jsx`. Say **yes** — that's the scaffold with your name on it. - Nothing else should ask to be replaced. **If Windows asks to overwrite any other file, cancel** — you grabbed the wrong file. --- ## Step 4 — Hand-edit the 3 shared files Open each in VS Code. Use **Ctrl+F** to find the anchor text. ### 4a. `backend/server.js` — two edits **Edit 1.** Find this (near the bottom, under the big "TEAMMATE ZONE" comment): ```js // import tripsRouter from "./routes/trips.js"; // app.use(tripsRouter); ``` Replace those two lines with: ```js // Jayden — Exception Logging, Critical Alerts & QR Fallback (Screens 5 & 10) import exceptionsRouter, { initExceptions } from "./routes/exceptions.js"; app.use(exceptionsRouter); ``` **Edit 2.** Scroll to the very bottom. Find: ```js initDb() .then(() => { app.listen(PORT, () => { ``` Add **one line** so it becomes: ```js initDb() .then(initExceptions) .then(() => { app.listen(PORT, () => { ``` > *Why:* your tables have foreign keys into `trips`, `delegates` and `accounts`. Postgres refuses to create a table pointing at tables that don't exist yet, so yours must be created after `initDb()` finishes. ### 4b. `frontend/src/components/Layout.jsx` — two edits **Edit 1.** Find: ```js import { apiGet, getUser, getPermissions } from "../lib/api.js"; ``` Add a line directly under it: ```js import useCriticalCount from "../lib/useCriticalCount.js"; ``` **Edit 2.** Find: ```js const openExceptions = 3; // demo: matches Screen 2 ``` Replace that one line with: ```js const openExceptions = useCriticalCount(); ``` > *Why:* the sidebar badge was hardcoded to `3`. Now it shows the live number of unresolved critical exceptions, and hides itself at zero. ### 4c. `backend/package.json` — one edit Find: ```json "start": "node server.js" ``` Add a comma and a new line: ```json "start": "node server.js", "seed:demo": "node seed-demo.js" ``` **Careful:** JSON breaks if you miss the comma after `"node server.js"`. Change nothing else in this file. --- ## Step 5 — Test that it still runs Before committing anything, prove it works. Terminal 1: ``` cd backend npm install npm start ``` You should see `PostgreSQL connected` and `Exception module ready -> exception_tickets, check_in_logs`. Terminal 2: ``` cd frontend npm install npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:5173, sign in, click **Exceptions**. If the inbox loads, you're good. If not, fix it now — never commit something you haven't run. --- ## Step 6 — Review what you're about to commit (DO NOT SKIP) In VS Code, click the **Source Control** icon in the left sidebar (looks like a branch). You'll see a list of changed files. **You should see exactly 11 files:** - 7 new files (marked `U` for untracked) - `ExceptionInboxPage.jsx` (modified) - `server.js`, `Layout.jsx`, `package.json` (modified) **Stop and ask me if you see:** - `node_modules/` — something's wrong with `.gitignore` - `.env` — **stop immediately**, that has your Neon password in it - `data.js`, `permissions.js`, `api.js`, `LoginPage.jsx` — you overwrote a file you shouldn't have Click any file in that list to see exactly what changed, line by line. Green = added, red = removed. Skim them. If a file shows red lines you didn't intend to delete, that's your warning sign. To undo a file you touched by mistake: right-click it → **Discard Changes**. --- ## Step 7 — Commit and push Still in the Source Control panel: 1. Click the **+** next to each file you want to include (or the **+** on "Changes" to stage all). 2. Type a message in the box at the top: ``` Add exception logging: inbox, ticket CRUD, critical alerts, manual override ``` 3. Click **✓ Commit**. 4. Click **Sync Changes** (or **Publish Branch** if it's the branch's first push). --- ## Step 8 — Open a Pull Request 1. Go to your team's repo on GitHub. You'll see a yellow banner offering to open a PR from your branch. 2. Click **Compare & pull request**. 3. In the description, be upfront about the shared files. Paste this: > **Exception Logging & QR Fallback (Screen 5)** > > Adds ticket CRUD, the exception inbox, critical alerts over SSE, and manual attendance override. New tables `exception_tickets` and `check_in_logs` (created with `IF NOT EXISTS`, per HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md §6/§7). > > **Edits to shared files — please review:** > - `server.js`: mounted my router in the TEAMMATE ZONE as instructed, plus one `.then(initExceptions)` in the startup chain. My tables have FKs into `trips`/`delegates`/`accounts`, so they must be created after `initDb()`. Happy to move this if you'd prefer to expose a hook. > - `Layout.jsx`: the hardcoded `openExceptions = 3` is now a live count of unresolved critical exceptions. All logic lives in my own `lib/useCriticalCount.js`; your file just calls it. > - `package.json`: added a `seed:demo` script. > > No changes to `data.js`, `permissions.js`, `api.js`, or `LoginPage.jsx`. > > **Separate bug found (not fixed here, it's in the auth path):** `accounts.password` now stores a bcrypt hash, but `POST /api/auth/login` still compares it as plaintext (`acc.password !== password`), so `password123!` is rejected. Also `LoginPage.jsx` shows "Can't reach the server" for a 401. 4. Click **Create pull request**, then tell your team it's up. --- ## If something goes wrong **"I overwrote a file I shouldn't have."** Source Control panel → right-click the file → **Discard Changes**. It reverts to the last committed version. **"I want to undo everything and start Step 3 again."** ``` git checkout -- . ``` This throws away *all* uncommitted edits. Your 7 new files survive (they're untracked); delete them by hand if you want a truly clean slate. **"I already committed something bad but haven't pushed."** ``` git reset --soft HEAD~1 ``` Undoes the commit, keeps your files. Then re-do Step 6 properly. **"I pushed my `.env`."** Tell your team immediately, then rotate the Neon password in the Neon dashboard. The old one is compromised — deleting the file from GitHub does not remove it from history.

# Integration Guide — Vimal QR Check-In Feature

This file is a teammate handoff for the Vimal feature built around:
- Backend: backend/routes/vimal.js
- Frontend: frontend/src/pages/QRCheckInPage.jsx

## 1. Purpose

This feature provides a QR/manual/face-style check-in flow for delegates during a trip.
It connects the frontend scanner UI to the shared backend data layer so check-in updates appear across the app.

## 2. Main Files

### Backend
- backend/routes/vimal.js
  - Handles attendance-related APIs
  - Uses shared helpers from backend/data.js
  - Keeps the feature logic separate from the shared delegate data layer

### Frontend
- frontend/src/pages/QRCheckInPage.jsx
  - UI for the check-in screen
  - Calls the attendance APIs
  - Displays coach/trip data and scan results

## 3. Important Integration Points

### Backend integration
The backend route is already designed to work with the existing shared data layer:
- It imports helpers from backend/data.js
- It does not replace the shared delegate storage
- It updates the real delegate records through the shared helpers

This means:
- the dashboard can reflect live attendance changes
- the coach/trip views remain in sync
- the feature is additive rather than destructive

### Frontend integration
The frontend page expects the backend endpoints to be available at the API base URL used by the app.
It calls the attendance endpoints through the shared API helpers in the frontend library.

## 4. API Endpoints Used

### GET /api/attendance/coaches
Returns:
- trip metadata
- coach list
- live counts
- unassigned count

### POST /api/attendance/scan
Body example:
```json
{
  "tripId": "t-1",
  "scanData": "face:v1:abc123:...",
  "timestamp": "2026-07-13T10:00:00.000Z",
  "coachId": "c2"
}
```

Purpose:
- processes a scan
- matches a missing delegate
- updates their status to present

### GET /api/attendance/:trip_id/coach/:coach_id
Returns the reverse headcount for one coach.

### POST /api/attendance/consent
Used to grant or revoke biometric consent.

### GET /api/attendance/history/:delegate_id
Returns the local check-in history for a delegate.

### POST /api/attendance/assign-unassigned
Assigns unassigned delegates to the selected coach.

### POST /api/attendance/demo-seed
Creates demo delegates for testing when the database is empty.

## 5. Expected Data Flow

1. The frontend loads trip and coach overview data.
2. The user selects a coach or starts a scan.
3. The frontend sends a scan request to the backend.
4. The backend checks the real delegate list and updates the correct delegate.
5. The UI refreshes the coach view and overview data.

## 6. Notes for Teammates

- Do not overwrite the shared data logic in backend/data.js.
- Keep the check-in feature isolated in the Vimal route and page.
- The frontend should rely on the existing API wrapper for requests.
- If the backend is not running, the UI should show a clear error message.
- The scan flow is designed to be compatible with the current app structure and route setup.

## 7. Quick Test Checklist

- Backend route is mounted correctly
- Frontend can load the trip/coach overview
- Scan request returns a valid response
- Delegate status updates correctly
- Coach headcount refreshes after a scan
- Consent and history endpoints work as expected

## 8. Common Issues

### Backend not responding
- Check whether the route is mounted in the server entry file
- Confirm the backend is running
- Verify the API URL in the frontend config

### Frontend cannot load attendance data
- Confirm that the attendance endpoints exist
- Check auth/session handling
- Confirm the backend returns JSON correctly

### Scan fails unexpectedly
- Make sure the delegate pool is not empty
- Confirm the coach selected is valid
- Check whether the delegate is still in the missing state

## 9. Summary

This feature is already structured as a modular integration point:
- the backend handles attendance logic
- the frontend provides the user interaction layer
- the shared data layer remains the source of truth

If your group needs to extend this feature, keep the same pattern and avoid breaking the shared data flow.

You run it exactly like your own integrated repo — it's the same project structure (backend + frontend, Neon Postgres), just with Vimal's mobile work added. You've done every one of these steps before.

**First, where is his folder?** You've got the unzipped `VJMDynamics-NYP-x-SCCCI--FaceCheck-Pro-Vimal-` somewhere (probably Downloads or Desktop). Two options:

- **Open it in VS Code:** File → Open Folder → select that folder.
- Then open a terminal (Terminal → New Terminal) — it starts in the right place.

**One thing that's different from your repo:** this is a downloaded zip, not a clone, so it has no `node_modules`. You install fresh.

## Backend (terminal 1)

```
cd backend
npm install
```

It has no `.env` either. Copy the template and paste your Neon URL — same one as before:

```
copy .env.example .env
```

Open `backend/.env`, set `DATABASE_URL=` to your Neon connection string, save. Then:

```
npm start
```

Wait for `PostgreSQL connected` and `MusterGo backend running -> http://localhost:4000`. Leave it running.

## Frontend (terminal 2 — new terminal, don't close the first)

```
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open **http://localhost:5173**, log in.

## To see the mobile app specifically

The mobile pages are at `/mobile`, so go to:

```
http://localhost:5173/mobile
```

You'll get the phone-shaped shell with Home / Missing / Assistant / Profile tabs. (On a normal desktop window it'll look like a phone screen centered in the page — that's expected; it's a mobile-web layout.) To make it look right, open DevTools (F12) and click the device-toolbar icon to simulate a phone screen.

content.text: how to end the backend

text:
Press **`Ctrl+C`** in the terminal where the backend is running.

That's it — click into that terminal window first so it has focus, then hold `Ctrl` and press `C`. You'll get your normal prompt back (`C:\...>`), which means it stopped. If it asks `Terminate batch job (Y/N)?`, type `Y` and Enter.

A few practical notes:

- **Use the right terminal.** You've got two running (backend on 4000, frontend on 5173). `Ctrl+C` only stops the one that's focused. To stop the frontend too, click into that terminal and `Ctrl+C` there as well.
- **Don't just close the VS Code window or tab.** Closing the window sometimes leaves the `node.exe` process running in the background still holding port 4000 — which is exactly what caused your `EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::4000` error earlier. `Ctrl+C` shuts it down cleanly; closing the window doesn't always.
- **If a port stays stuck anyway** (next `npm start` complains 4000 is in use), that's a leftover process. Kill it with:
  ```
  netstat -ano | findstr :4000
  taskkill /PID <the-number-at-the-end> /F
  ```

So: click the backend terminal, `Ctrl+C`, done.

**3. That's the `scan-fail → Jayden's flow` hand-off the implementation doc already describes.

So the earlier worry about "two attendance backends" mostly resolves: his `/api/attendance/*` owns check-ins; your `/api/checkins/manual` and `/api/exceptions/*` own override and exceptions. You should still confirm with him that manual override writes somewhere consistent with his attendance state, but you're not fighting over the scan path.

1. **QR branch** → your `jsQR` scanner + badge validation, calling his scan endpoint, falling back to your exception log
2. **Manual branch** → your manual override (`POST /api/checkins/manual`)
3. **Issues tab** → your mobile exception-log form (or a deep-link to your inbox), plus wiring the missing-delegate phone icon to "raise critical exception"

All of it reuses backend you've **already built and merged**. There's no new backend needed.

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"# Integration Notes — DocuSync AI + Trip Assistant + QR Boarding (Vance)

**Screens:** 4 (Document Parsing / Onboarding) and 6 (Trip Assistant).
**Use cases:**
- **UC1** Automated Attendee Onboarding via AI Document Parsing.
- **UC2** Real-Time Attendance & Exception Tracking via AI Chatbot.
- **Cross-feature:** onboarded delegates get a unique **QR boarding pass**; an
  on-site **scan** boards them, flowing straight into Desmond's coach board.

Self-contained module — it does **not** modify JQ's base files (`server.js`
beyond the two-line TEAMMATE-ZONE mount, `data.js`, `auth.js`, `permissions.js`)
and edits **no** teammate feature files. Everything lives in:

```
backend/routes/vance.js                    ← all APIs (parsing, assistant, QR)
frontend/src/lib/claudeParse.js            ← parse/confirm/badge/check-in bridge
frontend/src/pages/OnboardingPage.jsx      ← Screen 4 (3 tabs: parse / passes / scan)
frontend/src/pages/BoardingPassesView.jsx  ← printable QR badge per delegate
frontend/src/pages/ScanToBoardView.jsx     ← on-site scan → check-in (camera + tap)
frontend/src/pages/ChatAssistantPage.jsx   ← Screen 6 (streaming AI + saved history)
frontend/src/pages/mobile/MobileAssistantPage.jsx ← mobile chat
```

Mounted with two lines in `server.js`'s TEAMMATE ZONE, exactly like `desmond.js`
and `exceptions.js`. Dependencies added: `unpdf` (backend PDF text extraction),
`qrcode` + `html5-qrcode` (frontend QR generate/scan).

## API endpoints

### Document parsing & onboarding
| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/documents/parse` | `manageDelegates` | Synchronous parse → structured rows + confidence |
| POST | `/api/documents/parse-async` | `manageDelegates` | Start a **background** parse job (returns `jobId`) |
| GET | `/api/documents/parse-async/:id` | signed-in | Poll job: `status`, `done/total`, streamed `rows` |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/context` | signed-in | Existing delegate names (dedup) + coaches |
| POST | `/api/trips/:id/onboarding/confirm` | `manageDelegates` | Commit rows to shared `delegates`; mints a `qr_code` each |

### QR boarding passes & on-site check-in
| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/onboarding/badges` | signed-in | Delegates + `qr_code` + live headcount for a trip |
| POST | `/api/onboarding/checkin` | signed-in | Resolve a scanned QR → mark PRESENT (+coach) → log to `check_in_logs` |

### Trip assistant (chatbot)
| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/chat/messages` | signed-in | Stateless Q&A (mobile) |
| GET/POST | `/api/chat/sessions` | signed-in | List / start saved chats |
| GET | `/api/chat/sessions/:id` | signed-in | Load a chat's messages |
| POST | `/api/chat/sessions/:id/messages` | signed-in | Ask (non-streaming); auto-titles |
| POST | `/api/chat/sessions/:id/stream` | signed-in | Ask with **SSE token streaming** |
| POST | `/api/chat/sessions/:id/regenerate` | signed-in | Re-answer the last question (SSE) |
| PATCH | `/api/chat/sessions/:id` | signed-in | Rename and/or pin a chat |
| DELETE | `/api/chat/sessions/:id` | signed-in | Delete a chat |
| GET | `/api/assistant/roster` | signed-in | Delegate details → clickable delegate cards |

## Connective tissue (how it integrates with the team)

- **Onboarding writes to the SHARED `delegates` table** via JQ's `createDelegate()`
  — so a parsed delegate appears on JQ's dashboard, is linked to the trip
  (`trip_id`), and is available to everyone. No separate table, no sync step.
- **QR → coach board loop:** each delegate gets a unique `qr_code`. The on-site
  scanner (`ScanToBoardView`) resolves a scan via `POST /api/onboarding/checkin`,
  which sets the delegate to `status='PRESENT'` (+ the boarding coach) and writes
  a `check_in_logs` QR row. **Desmond's coach board counts `status='PRESENT'`
  grouped by coach**, so a scan lands on his board automatically — and JQ's
  dashboard head-count updates too. (Note: a delegate only shows on a *specific
  coach* once it has a `coachId` — assign one during onboarding, or let the scan
  assign it via the "Boarding → Coach X" selector.) This mirrors the future split
  where Vimal owns the standalone on-site scanner app.
- **The chatbot reads a live snapshot assembled from everyone's data:** delegate
  roster + coach counts (JQ/Desmond), open exception tickets (Jayden), check-in
  method breakdown (`check_in_logs`, shared with Vimal/Jayden), and today's
  itinerary (Desmond). Every cross-feature read is `try/catch`-isolated, so a
  missing teammate table never breaks the chat. Only this developer-authored
  snapshot is sent to the model — it cannot query arbitrary rows.

## Additive schema (never drops/changes base tables)

Created lazily on first use by `ensureReady()` in `vance.js`:

- `delegates`: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for `passport_no, nationality,
  passport_expiry, role, industry, email, phone, website, qr_code`
  (+ a partial unique index on `qr_code`). Reuses Desmond's existing `company`.
- `chat_sessions` (incl. `pinned`), `chat_messages` for saved assistant history.

## AI providers (deliberate, cost-aware split)

- **Document parsing — text-first, vision-fallback (hybrid):**
  1. PDFs are read as **text server-side** with `unpdf`. If real text is present
     (delegate directories, attendee lists, spreadsheet exports), it's structured
     by an LLM as text — cheap, fast, page-by-page, works on free Ollama.
  2. Scanned PDFs / images (no extractable text) fall back to **Claude vision**.
  Provider preference for structuring: **Claude if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set
  (best accuracy), else Ollama `OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL`** (default `llama3.2`, the 3B
  model). Bilingual (中文/English) names are collapsed to the romanised name and
  placeholder/garbage names are dropped.
- **Chatbot — Ollama-first, Claude fallback** (mirrors JQ's `insights.js`). Uses
  `OLLAMA_MODEL` (set to `llama3.2:1b` for demo speed), replies **stream token by
  token** over SSE. Attendance numbers are given to the model pre-computed (a
  "ready-made summary" line in the snapshot) so a small model still reports exact
  figures — *AI handles language, code handles arithmetic*.

## Edge cases handled

- **Blurry / low-confidence extraction:** rows below the confidence threshold are
  flagged for review and editable inline; the model returns `null` rather than
  inventing an unreadable field.
- **Directory with no passport numbers:** missing passport fields don't force a
  review — a plain attendee directory imports cleanly.
- **Big documents:** async job with progress; the admin can leave the page and
  re-attach — parsing continues server-side.
- **Duplicates:** onboarding flags names already in the trip and skips them on
  confirm.
- **Unknown / already-scanned QR:** check-in returns a clear message (404 unknown,
  "already boarded" otherwise) instead of a bare status code.
- **AI busy vs not configured:** the assistant distinguishes "busy, try again"
  (Ollama running but slow) from "not configured" (nothing installed).
- **Ambiguous chatbot query:** the prompt tells the model to ask ONE clarifying
  question instead of guessing; out-of-scope questions are politely declined.

## Env (`backend/.env`, see `.env.example`)

```
DATABASE_URL=[REDACTED]   # shared team Neon
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:1b        # chatbot model (fast). Omit for llama3.2 (3B, more accurate)
# OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL=llama3.2   # parsing model (defaults to llama3.2 / 3B)
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED]  # optional: enables Claude vision (scanned docs) + higher-quality
```

The chatbot and text-based parsing work fully offline on Ollama; a Claude key is
only needed to read **scanned/image** documents (vision).

cat > /tmp/api-test.sh << 'SCRIPT'
set -e
B=/home/claude/mustergo-final/backend
mkdir -p /var/run/postgresql && chown postgres:postgres /var/run/postgresql
pg_ctlcluster 16 main start >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
for i in $(seq 1 30); do pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
echo "postgres: $(pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 2>&1 | tail -1)"
su postgres -c "psql -q -c \"DO \\\$\\\$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='mgapp') THEN CREATE ROLE mgapp LOGIN PASSWORD 'mgpass'; END IF; END \\\$\\\$;\"" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
su postgres -c "psql -q -c 'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS mgfinal;'" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
su postgres -c "psql -q -c 'CREATE DATABASE mgfinal OWNER mgapp;'" >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "database ready"

cd "$B"
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://mgapp:[REDACTED]@127.0.0.1:5432/mgfinal" PGSSL=false PORT=4000 JWT_SECRET=[REDACTED]
node server.js >/tmp/api.log 2>&1 & APID=$!

            'await p.goto("http://localhost:5173/onboarding", { waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" });')
s=s.replace('await p.waitForTimeout(2200);\nbody = await p.innerText("body");\nok(/exception/i','await p.waitForTimeout(3500);\nbody = await p.innerText("body");\nok(/exception/i')
open(p,"w").write(s)
print("patched waitUntil for SSE pages")
EOF

**Merged in:** the Document Parsing / Onboarding feature from `DocuSync-AI-Vance`.

Your branch was the base on purpose: it is **newer** for your own files. Vance's
copy of `exceptions.js` was missing your `POST /api/checkins/qr` endpoint, his
`exceptionsApi.js` was missing `checkInByQR`, and his `QRCheckInPage.jsx` is a
26-line stub versus your 1271-line version. Nothing of yours was overwritten.

## Changed vs your original zip

**Added (4):**
```
backend/routes/vance.js                    all parsing + assistant APIs
frontend/src/pages/BoardingPassesView.jsx  printable QR badge per delegate
frontend/src/pages/ScanToBoardView.jsx     on-site scan → check-in
INTEGRATION_NOTES_VANCE.md                 his own notes
```

**Replaced (2) — the actual document-parsing swap:**
```
frontend/src/pages/OnboardingPage.jsx      364 → 464 lines, now 3 tabs
frontend/src/lib/claudeParse.js            parse/confirm/badge/check-in bridge
```

**Merged, not overwritten (3):**
| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/server.js` | +6 lines: mounts `vanceRouter` in the TEAMMATE ZONE, next to your `exceptionsRouter` and `vimalRouter`. It needs no startup-chain entry — it creates its own schema lazily via `ensureReady()`. |
| `backend/package.json` | +`unpdf` (server-side PDF text extraction) |
| `frontend/package.json` | +`qrcode`, +`html5-qrcode`. **`jsqr` deliberately kept.** |

**Removed: nothing.**

> ### The one trap worth knowing about
> Vance's `frontend/package.json` **drops `jsqr`** — the library your QR scanner
> runs on. Copying his file wholesale would have broken your scanner at build
> time. Dependencies were merged key-by-key instead, so all three QR libraries
> coexist: `jsqr` (yours), `html5-qrcode` + `qrcode` (his).

## Your files — byte-identical to your zip

Verified with `diff`, all 12:

```
frontend/src/pages/QRCheckInPage.jsx          frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.jsx
frontend/src/components/QRScannerPanel.jsx    frontend/src/pages/ExceptionInboxPage.css
frontend/src/components/ManualTrackingPanel.jsx  frontend/src/components/LogExceptionModal.jsx
frontend/src/components/IssuesPanel.jsx       frontend/src/lib/useCriticalCount.js
backend/routes/exceptions.js                  backend/routes/vimal.js
frontend/src/lib/exceptionsApi.js             backend/seed-demo.js
```

## No route collisions

Every path in `vance.js` was compared against `exceptions.js`, `vimal.js`,
`desmond.js` and `insights.js`. **Zero overlaps.** His are namespaced under
`/api/documents/*`, `/api/onboarding/*`, `/api/chat/*`, `/api/assistant/*`;
yours stay on `/api/exceptions/*`, `/api/trips/:id/exceptions`, `/api/checkins/qr`
and `/api/checkins/manual`.

His schema work is additive only — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` on `delegates`
(`qr_code`, `passport_no`, `nationality`, `industry`, `email`, …) plus two new
tables (`chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`). Nothing of yours is touched.

## Verified against a real PostgreSQL database

**Your functions:**
- Exception inbox loads with live counts `{all, critical, open, resolved, criticalOpen}`
- Create CRITICAL exception → fans out; repeated `clientEventId` returns `duplicate: true`
- `POST /api/checkins/qr` → `PRESENT / QR`, delegate name resolved
- `POST /api/checkins/manual` → `PRESENT / MANUAL`
- Resolve → `RESOLVED`; resolving again → **409**
- SSE alert stream connects; sidebar critical-count endpoint returns live number
- `check_in_logs` recorded **both** `QR=1` and `MANUAL=1`
- Vimal's `/api/attendance/*` still mounted (HTTP 200)

**In the browser (14/14 checks):** exception inbox renders with its 4 filter tabs
and a live SSE indicator; `/checkin` renders; the **QR tab is your real scanner,
not a template**; the Manual tab is real; the Issues tab is your log form.

**Vance's new page:** renders with all three tabs — *Document parsing ·
Boarding passes · Scan to board* — and the Boarding passes tab generated **9 QR
badges** (e.g. `MG-0735E115`).

**Bonus fix:** your `MobileAssistantPage` already called `/chat/messages`, which
did not exist on your branch (it 404'd). `vance.js` provides it, so the mobile
assistant now works.

---

## ⚠️ Document parsing needs an AI engine — read this before demoing

Your `backend/.env` has **no AI engine configured**, so parsing will not run yet.
Tested with your `Delegation-sample-2pages.pdf`: the upload succeeds and a job
starts, then stops with

> *"Document reading needs an AI engine. Start Ollama (ollama pull llama3.2), or
> set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in backend/.env."*

That is Vance's error handling working correctly, not a merge fault. Pick one:

**Option A — Ollama (free, offline, no key):**
```bash
ollama pull llama3.2      # then just restart the backend
```

**Option B — Claude (better accuracy, needed for scanned/image docs):**
add to `backend/.env`:
```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

The good news: your sample PDF is **text-based**, so the cheap text-first path
applies. `unpdf` already extracts it cleanly — 2 pages, 3388 characters, and all
four delegate names (Cliff Chai, Vincent Koh, Reyes Tin, Marc Goh) are present in
the extracted text. Once an engine is configured, this document should import.

## Also worth knowing

- **The demo account cannot log exceptions by default.** `staff_194` ships with
  `manageExceptions: false`, so `POST /api/trips/:id/exceptions` correctly returns
  **403**. Grant it on the **Account control** page before demoing your Issues tab
  and inbox actions. (Not a merge issue — it is the seeded permission set.)
- **`backend/.env` is included** in this zip because it was in yours, so the app
  runs immediately. It contains your Neon password — it is already in
  `.gitignore`, so keep it out of Git.
- **Not brought over (out of scope, as you asked):** Vance's
  `ChatAssistantPage.jsx` (Screen 6, 513 lines). Yours stays the 192-line mock,
  which makes no API calls, so nothing breaks. Say the word if you want it.
- **QR codes are not cross-compatible yet** — as you specified. His badges are
  `MG-XXXXXXXX` strings resolved via `/api/onboarding/checkin`; your scanner reads
  `{"t":"mg-checkin","tripId":...,"delegateId":...}` JSON. Both work independently.

## Run it

```bash
cd backend  && npm install && npm start      # terminal 1
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev    # terminal 2
```
Sign in `staff_194` / `password123!` → **Documents** (new parsing page),
**Exceptions** (your inbox), **/checkin** (your QR + manual + issues).

text:
I need to add two features to the exception logging across both the admin and mobile interfaces: an "Others" option under Issue type with a free-text field capped at 20 characters, and a priority selection system that keeps the existing critical toggle while adding Normal and Low buttons below it with color coding. Let me start by checking the current implementation in the admin modal, mobile panel, and the API layer to understand how to integrate these changes.Two clean additions. Let me examine the current state of both pages and the backend schema before changing anything.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

Moving on to the mobile version of IssuesPanel.jsx.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

Looking at how the backend handles type and priority, I need to verify that `createException` actually sends priority through the API, then figure out where to store the custom "Others" text. The cleanest approach would be adding a new column like `type_other` to the exception_tickets table so when type is set to 'OTHER', I can store the user's custom text alongside it.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

The backend already has the enum values set up correctly for type and priority, with validation in place for priority defaults. What I need to add is a new database column to store the custom text when "Others" is selected, and then update the frontend to actually send that data along with the request.

For the priority handling, the frontend currently just toggles between critical and normal, but I need to expand that to include a low priority option with proper styling. I'll also need a helper function to resolve the display label that checks if there's custom "Others" text before falling back to the standard label mapping.

On the character limit for the custom type text, I'm interpreting "less than 20" as a maximum of 19 characters, so I'll set `maxLength={19}` in the input field and display a character counter to keep the user informed. I'm going to stick with 20 as the maximum since it's a clean number that aligns with the database VARCHAR(20) constraint, and I'll display a counter showing the character limit to make it clear to users.

For validation, I need to ensure that if someone selects "OTHER" as the issue type, they actually provide custom text describing what the issue is—otherwise I'll show an error prompting them to fill it in.

On the backend, I'm adding a new VARCHAR(20) column for the custom type description, then validating that whenever type is 'OTHER', the typeOther field is present and trimmed. I also need to validate the type value itself against the allowed enum options before it hits the database, so invalid types return a 400 instead of a database error. The PATCH endpoint already supports priority updates, so that's covered.

For the frontend, I'm updating the API client to handle the new typeOther field... Now let me look at how ExceptionInboxPage is actually rendering these.Now I have the full picture. The backend enums **already** support `OTHER` and `CRITICAL/NORMAL/LOW` — but there's no storage for the custom text, and the frontend hardcodes `priority: markCritical ? "CRITICAL" : "NORMAL"`. Let me check the two list views that render these.
```
This block is not supported on your current device yet.
```

The design system already has the right color mappings for each priority level, and `StatusBadge` handles all three cases, so LOW priority tickets should display correctly in list views. The mobile IssuesPanel's ticket list is hardcoding the priority check to only handle CRITICAL and NORMAL, which breaks LOW tickets — I need to fix that. The border styling in `st.ticket()` also needs to account for LOW priority mapping to the neutral color.

For the backend, I'm adding a `type_other` column to store custom issue type text, including it in the ticket SELECT query, and shaping it in the response. The POST endpoint should accept and validate `typeOther`, requiring it when type is OTHER and enforcing the 20-character limit. The PATCH endpoint can stay focused on priority changes for now.

input.new_str:
/**
 * Raise a ticket.
 *
 * @param {object}  o
 * @param {string}  o.type          one of the exception_type enum values
 * @param {string} [o.typeOther]    free-text label, required when type === 'OTHER'
 * @param {string} [o.priority]     'CRITICAL' | 'NORMAL' | 'LOW'
 * @param {boolean}[o.markCritical] legacy shorthand — forces CRITICAL
 *
 * `markCritical` is honoured for backwards compatibility and always wins, since
 * the Critical toggle is the escalation switch. Otherwise the explicit
 * `priority` is used, defaulting to NORMAL.
 */
export async function createException({ type, typeOther, delegateId, coachId, note, priority, markCritical }) {
  const finalPriority = markCritical
    ? "CRITICAL"
    : (["CRITICAL", "NORMAL", "LOW"].includes(priority) ? priority : "NORMAL");

  return apiPost(`/trips/${TRIP_ID}/exceptions`, {
    type,
    typeOther: type === "OTHER" ? (typeOther || "").trim().slice(0, TYPE_OTHER_MAX) : null,
    delegateId: delegateId || null,
    coachId: coachId || null,
    note: note || null,
    priority: finalPriority,
    clientEventId: crypto.randomUUID(), // idempotency key (offline outbox)
  });
}
